house-of-bourbon-parma.s: The House of Bourbon-Parma is a branch of the Spanish Bourbons founded by Philip, a son of Philip V of Spain and Elisabeth Farnese, who became Duke of Parma in 1748 under the Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle. The family ruled Parma until 1802, Lucca from 1815 to 1847 and Parma again…

house-of-griffins.s: The House of Griffin was the dynasty that ruled the Duchy of Pomerania from the 12th century until 1637. Its first historically attested member was Wartislaw I, who accepted Christianity in the 1120s.

house-of-borgia.s: The House of Borgia was a noble family of Valencian origin (Borja) that rose to great power in Renaissance Italy. It produced two popes, Callixtus III (1455–1458) and Alexander VI (1492–1503), whose children Cesare and Lucrezia Borgia became notorious in politics and legend.

house-of-carafa.s: The House of Carafa was a powerful noble family of the Kingdom of Naples, holding many fiefs and princely titles from the late Middle Ages. Its most famous member, Gian Pietro Carafa, became Pope Paul IV (1555–1559), a stern leader of the Counter-Reformation whose nephews were…

hersekzade-ahmed-pasha.s: Hersekzade Ahmed Pasha was an Ottoman statesman and admiral, born a son of Stjepan Vukčić Kosača, Herceg of Saint Sava. Taken to the Ottoman court as a youth, he converted to Islam and married a daughter of Sultan Bayezid II.

hildburghausen.s: Hildburghausen is a small town in southern Thuringia, Germany, near the Bavarian border. From 1680 to 1826 it was the residence of the dukes of Saxe-Hildburghausen, whose daughter Therese married the future King Ludwig I of Bavaria in 1810.

hans-von-bulow.s: Hans von Bülow was a German conductor and pianist, one of the first virtuoso conductors. He conducted the premieres of Wagner's Tristan und Isolde (1865) and Die Meistersinger (1868), even after his wife Cosima left him for Wagner.

hedeby.s: Hedeby was a Viking Age trading town at the head of the Schlei inlet in Schleswig, now in northern Germany. From the eighth to the eleventh century it was one of the largest towns in Scandinavia, linking Baltic and North Sea trade and protected by the Danevirke.

hrvojes-missal.s: Hrvoje's Missal is a Croatian liturgical book written in the Glagolitic script around 1403–1404 in Split for Hrvoje Vukčić Hrvatinić, Grand Duke of Bosnia and Duke of Split. Copied by the scribe Butko, it is richly illuminated with miniatures in a mixed Gothic and Byzantine…

hohenstaufen.s: The Hohenstaufen, or Staufer, were a Swabian dynasty named after their castle on the Hohenstaufen mountain. Dukes of Swabia from 1079, they became German kings with Conrad III in 1138 and emperors with Frederick Barbarossa, Henry VI and Frederick II, who also ruled the Kingdom…

house-of-lobkowicz.s: The House of Lobkowicz is a Bohemian noble family recorded from the fourteenth century, raised to princely rank in 1624. Its members included the chancellor Zdeněk Vojtěch Popel of Lobkowicz and Prince Václav Eusebius, who acquired the Duchy of Sagan in 1646.

house-of-auersperg.s: The House of Auersperg is an Austrian noble family originating in Carniola, at the castle of Auersperg (Turjak) in present-day Slovenia. Its members served the Habsburgs as soldiers and statesmen, and in 1653 the line of Johann Weikhard von Auersperg was raised to princely rank.

hampshire.s: Hampshire is a county on the south coast of England, including the ports of Southampton and Portsmouth and the New Forest. Its old capital, Winchester, was the chief royal city of the kingdom of Wessex.

hengistbury-head.s: Hengistbury Head is a headland on the south coast of England beside Christchurch Harbour, now in Dorset. In the 1st century BCE it was one of the main ports of southern Britain, trading with Armorica and receiving Italian wine amphorae, while exporting metals, grain and cattle.

hod-hill.s: Hod Hill is a large Iron Age hillfort near Blandford Forum in Dorset, England, and one of the strongholds of the Durotriges. After the Roman invasion of 43 CE it was captured, and a Roman fort was built inside one corner of its ramparts, garrisoned by legionaries and auxiliary…

hooghly-river.s: The Hooghly is a distributary of the Ganges in West Bengal, India, flowing about 260 kilometres south past Kolkata to the Bay of Bengal. In the 17th and 18th centuries its banks were lined with European trading settlements, among them Portuguese Bandel, Dutch Chinsurah, French…

huguenots.s: The Huguenots were French Protestants of the Reformed, or Calvinist, tradition. They fought the French Wars of Religion from 1562 and gained toleration under the Edict of Nantes in 1598.

hortus-malabaricus.s: Hortus Malabaricus is a twelve-volume study of the plants of the Malabar Coast of India, published in Amsterdam between 1678 and 1693. It was compiled under Hendrik van Rheede, Dutch commander of Malabar, with Indian physicians and scholars including Itty Achuden.

hakon-sigurdsson.s: Håkon Sigurdsson, known as Haakon Jarl, was Earl of Lade who ruled most of Norway from about 975 to 995 under the overlordship of Harald Bluetooth of Denmark, and later independently. A firm supporter of the old Norse gods, he defeated the Jomsvikings at the Battle of…

hakon-eiriksson.s: Håkon Eiriksson was the last Earl of Lade, a grandson of Håkon Sigurdsson. He ruled part of Norway with his uncle Sweyn from 1012 until Olaf Haraldsson drove him out in 1015.

hunald-i-of-aquitaine.s: Hunald was Duke of Aquitaine from 735, succeeding his father Odo the Great. He resisted the authority of Charles Martel and his sons Carloman and Pippin the Short, who campaigned against him repeatedly.

hor-aha.s: Hor-Aha was a king of the First Dynasty of Egypt, around 3100 BCE, the successor of Narmer, and is often identified with Menes, the legendary first king. Labels from his reign record campaigns and religious foundations, and tradition credits him with the founding of Memphis.

house-of-tudor.s: The House of Tudor was the royal family of Welsh origin that ruled England and Ireland from 1485 to 1603. Its monarchs were Henry VII, Henry VIII, Edward VI, Mary I and Elizabeth I.

haeburu.s: Haeburu is a king of Buyeo in Korean tradition who, according to the Samguk sagi, moved his court east on divine advice and founded Eastern Buyeo, traditionally in 86 BCE. The legend says he found the child Geumwa, who succeeded him.

hasan-bughra-khan.s: Hasan Bughra Khan, also called Harun, was a ruler of the Kara-Khanid Khanate in Central Asia in the late 10th century. In 992 he led his army against the declining Samanid Empire and briefly occupied its capital, Bukhara, but fell ill and died while withdrawing.

hadad.s: Hadad was the storm and weather god of the ancient Semitic peoples of Syria and Mesopotamia, known in Akkadian as Adad. Attested as Hadda in the archives of Ebla in the 3rd millennium BCE, he was worshipped at Aleppo and across the Levant, where he was later identified with Baal.

henry-townsend.s: Henry Townsend was an English missionary of the Church Missionary Society who worked among the Yoruba from the 1840s. He settled at Abeokuta in 1846, founded churches and schools, and in 1859 started Iwe Irohin, one of the first newspapers in Nigeria, printed in Yoruba.

herakleopolis-magna.s: Herakleopolis Magna was an ancient Egyptian city south of the Faiyum, near modern Beni Suef, and capital of the 20th nome of Upper Egypt. Around 2160 BCE its rulers founded the Ninth and Tenth Dynasties, which ruled much of Egypt in the First Intermediate Period until…

hezekiah.s: Hezekiah was king of Judah from about 715 to 686 BCE, remembered in the Hebrew Bible as a reformer who centralised worship in Jerusalem. He joined a revolt against Assyria and prepared Jerusalem by cutting the Siloam tunnel to bring water inside the walls.

heidelberg.s: Heidelberg is a city on the Neckar in Baden-Württemberg, south-western Germany. It was the residence of the electors palatine of the Rhine from the 13th century until 1720, and its university, founded by Rupert I in 1386, is the oldest in present-day Germany.

henry-of-laach.s: Henry of Laach was a German nobleman who is the first person recorded with the title count palatine of the Rhine, around 1085 to 1087. Earlier counts palatine of Lotharingia had served as royal deputies in the Rhineland, and Henry moved the office's centre to the middle Rhine.

herrenhausen-gardens.s: The Herrenhausen Gardens in Hanover, Germany, surround the former summer palace of the electors of Hanover. The Great Garden, one of the most important Baroque formal gardens in Europe, was laid out from 1666 and much enlarged under Electress Sophia, who took a close interest…

holy-robe.s: The Holy Robe is a relic kept in Trier Cathedral and venerated as the seamless tunic worn by Jesus before the crucifixion. Tradition says Empress Helena sent it to Trier; it is first clearly documented in the 12th century and was first shown publicly to pilgrims in 1512.

hellanodikai.s: The Hellanodikai, 'judges of the Greeks', were the officials who organised and judged the ancient Olympic Games. Chosen from the citizens of Elis, they supervised the athletes' training, enforced the rules, fined offenders and awarded the olive wreaths.

hippias-of-elis.s: Hippias of Elis was a Greek sophist of the late 5th century BCE, a contemporary of Socrates. He served Elis as an envoy and was famous for his wide learning in mathematics, astronomy, history and the arts, and for his powerful memory.

hippias-tyrant.s: Hippias was tyrant of Athens from 527 to 510 BCE, the eldest son of Peisistratos. After his brother Hipparchus was murdered in 514 BCE his rule grew harsh, and he was expelled with Spartan help in 510.

herault-river.s: The Hérault is a river in southern France, about 150 kilometres long, rising in the Cévennes and flowing south past Ganges and Pézenas to the Mediterranean at Agde, a Greek foundation near its mouth. In antiquity it roughly marked the boundary between the Elisyces of the…

hazarajat.s: The Hazarajat is the mountainous central region of Afghanistan, homeland of the Hazara people, centred on Bamiyan and the highlands of the upper Helmand. Largely self-governing until the 1890s, it was conquered by Emir Abdur Rahman Khan in brutal campaigns between 1891 and…

heraklion.s: Heraklion is the largest city and capital of Crete. It was founded in the 820s as Chandax, the fortified capital of the Andalusi Arab emirate that ruled the island until the Byzantine general Nikephoros Phokas took it in 961.

hashimids-of-derbent.s: The Hashimids of Derbent were an Arab dynasty that ruled the city of Derbent on the Caspian coast as hereditary emirs from 869 to 1075. Founded by the governor Hashim ibn Suraqa as Abbasid authority weakened, the family gradually became a local power, fighting and allying with…

hail.s: Ha'il is a city in north-central Saudi Arabia, capital of Ha'il Province, between the Aja and Salma mountains. It was the capital of the Rashidi Emirate of Jabal Shammar from 1836, a stop on pilgrim and caravan routes, and in the late 19th century the seat of the most powerful…

hamdanid-dynasty.s: The Hamdanid dynasty was an Arab Shia family of the Banu Taghlib that ruled emirates in northern Iraq and Syria in the 10th century. One branch held Mosul, while Sayf al-Dawla founded the emirate of Aleppo in 945 and led constant wars against Byzantium.

haiphong.s: Haiphong is a port city in northern Vietnam, on the Red River delta near the Gulf of Tonkin, and one of the country's largest cities. Developed by the French as the port of Tonkin, it was shelled by the French navy in November 1946, an event that helped start the First…

harmonia.s: Harmonia was a goddess of Greek myth, the daughter of Ares and Aphrodite and the wife of Cadmus, founder of Thebes. The gods attended their wedding, at which she received a necklace that brought misfortune to all who later owned it.

hecataeus-of-miletus.s: Hecataeus of Miletus was an early Greek historian and geographer. His Periodos Ges, a description of the known world arranged as a coastal voyage, and his Genealogies, which treated myths critically, survive only in fragments quoted by later writers.

heraclitus.s: Heraclitus was a Greek philosopher of Ephesus who lived around 500 BCE. His book of sayings, known only from fragments, taught that the world is in constant change, summed up in the later phrase that everything flows, and that it is governed by an underlying order, the logos,…

hamid-idris-awate.s: Hamid Idris Awate was an Eritrean fighter regarded as the father of Eritrea's armed struggle for independence. On 1 September 1961, at Mount Adal in western Eritrea, he and a small band fired the first shots of the war against Ethiopian rule under the banner of the Eritrean…

histiaea.s: Histiaea was an ancient Greek city in northern Euboea, controlling the strait facing Thessaly. After it revolted against Athens in 446 BCE, Pericles expelled its inhabitants and replaced them with Athenian settlers, and the town became known as Oreus.

helos.s: Helos was an ancient town in southern Laconia, in the marshy plain near the mouth of the Eurotas river, mentioned in Homer's Catalogue of Ships. Ancient tradition derived the name of the helots, the state serfs of Sparta, from its inhabitants, said to have been enslaved after…

heimskringla.s: Heimskringla is a collection of sagas of the kings of Norway written in Old Norse around 1230, usually attributed to the Icelandic historian Snorri Sturluson. Beginning with the legendary Yngling kings, it runs through Harald Fairhair, Olaf Tryggvason and Saint Olaf to the…

hans-kelsen.s: Hans Kelsen was an Austrian jurist and legal philosopher, the author of the Pure Theory of Law, which treated law as a hierarchy of norms separate from politics and morals. He was the principal drafter of the Austrian federal constitution of 1920, which created the first…

hamburger-bank.s: The Hamburger Bank was a public giro bank founded by the city of Hamburg in 1619, modelled on the Exchange Bank of Amsterdam. It kept accounts in a stable unit of account, the mark banco, backed by deposited silver, which made Hamburg a leading centre of payments in northern…

holstentor.s: The Holstentor is a brick Gothic city gate of Lübeck, built between 1464 and 1478 to guard the western approach to the city. Its two round towers became a symbol of the city and of the Hanseatic League, and it now houses a museum of the city's history.

henri-giraud.s: Henri Giraud was a French general who escaped from German captivity in both world wars, his escape from Königstein fortress in 1942 making him famous. After the Allied landings in North Africa he became French high commissioner and commander in Algiers, and in 1943 he…

holy-cross-abbey-donauworth.s: Holy Cross Abbey in Donauwörth, Bavaria, was a monastery founded in the early 11th century by the lords of Werd to house a relic of the True Cross brought from Constantinople, and a Benedictine abbey from around 1100. It remained Catholic when most of the town became Lutheran,…

hellweg.s: The Hellweg was a medieval trade and military road in Westphalia running from the Rhine near Duisburg east through Essen, Dortmund, Soest and Paderborn towards the Weser. Towns along it prospered from trade, and the fertile loess belt it followed is still known as the Hellweg…

haguenau-forest.s: The Haguenau Forest is one of the largest forests in France, covering about 190 square kilometres in northern Alsace around the town of Haguenau. The Hohenstaufen emperors used it as a hunting ground from their castle at Haguenau, and it was long called the Holy Forest because…

heilbronn-league.s: The Heilbronn League was an alliance formed at Heilbronn in April 1633 between Sweden and the Protestant estates of the Franconian, Swabian and Rhenish circles, led by the Swedish chancellor Axel Oxenstierna after the death of Gustavus Adolphus. It financed the Swedish war in…

haut-rhin.s: Haut-Rhin is a department of eastern France covering southern Alsace, with Colmar as its prefecture and Mulhouse as its largest city. Created in 1790, it was annexed by Germany with the rest of Alsace from 1871 to 1918, apart from the Territoire de Belfort, which remained French.

hans-sachs.s: Hans Sachs was a shoemaker and poet of Nuremberg, the most famous of the Meistersinger, the guild-trained poet-singers of German cities. He wrote thousands of songs, plays and poems, and his The Wittenberg Nightingale of 1523 welcomed Martin Luther's teaching.

heinrich-parler.s: Heinrich Parler was a German master builder from Cologne who worked in Schwäbisch Gmünd, where from 1351 he built the choir of the Holy Cross Minster, one of the first late Gothic hall churches in Germany. He founded the Parler family of architects and sculptors; his son Peter…

heller-coin.s: The Heller was a German coin first struck at the imperial mint of Schwäbisch Hall in the 12th century as a silver pfennig, the Haller pfennig, from which its name comes. It spread across the Empire, gradually losing value until it was worth half a pfennig, and survived as a…

heinkel.s: Heinkel was a German aircraft maker founded by Ernst Heinkel at Warnemünde in 1922 and based in Rostock. It built the He 111 bomber, a mainstay of the Luftwaffe in the Second World War, and the He 178 of 1939, the first aircraft to fly on a turbojet engine.

huliaipole.s: Huliaipole is a town in Zaporizhzhia Oblast in south-eastern Ukraine. It was the birthplace and headquarters of the anarchist Nestor Makhno, whose Revolutionary Insurrectionary Army of Ukraine was based there during the Russian Civil War of 1917–1921.

ho-chi-minh-city.s: Ho Chi Minh City, long known as Saigon, is the largest city of Vietnam, on the Saigon River near the Mekong delta. A Khmer settlement taken over by Vietnamese in the 17th century, it was captured by France in 1859 and became the capital of French Cochinchina and later of South…

ham-nghi.s: Hàm Nghi was emperor of Vietnam of the Nguyễn dynasty from 1884 to 1885. Enthroned at thirteen, he fled the capital Huế in July 1885 with the regent Tôn Thất Thuyết after a failed attack on the French, and his name was used to rally the Cần Vương resistance movement.

hon-gai.s: Hòn Gai is a town on Ha Long Bay in Quảng Ninh province, northern Vietnam, now the central part of Ha Long city. Under French rule it was the centre of the Hon Gai coalfield, worked from the late 1880s by the French Tonkin Coal Company, which made anthracite one of Indochina's…

habib-bourguiba.s: Habib Bourguiba was the leader of Tunisia's independence movement and the country's first president, from 1957 to 1987. A lawyer trained in Paris, he founded the Neo-Destour party in 1934, was repeatedly imprisoned by the French and negotiated independence in 1956, becoming…

hashimoto-sanai.s: Hashimoto Sanai was a Japanese physician and reformist samurai of the Fukui domain. Trained in Dutch medicine and Western learning, he became an adviser to the daimyo Matsudaira Yoshinaga and argued for opening Japan, strengthening its defences and choosing a capable shogunal…

hamaj.s: The Hamaj were a people of the southern Blue Nile region of Sudan whose leaders ruled the Funj Sultanate of Sennar as hereditary regents from 1761. Their founder, Muhammad Abu Likaylik, deposed Sultan Badi IV, and the Hamaj regents kept the Funj sultans as figureheads while…

hydatius.s: Hydatius was a bishop of Aquae Flaviae, modern Chaves, in the Roman province of Gallaecia. His Latin chronicle, continuing that of Jerome to the year 468, is the main contemporary source for the Suebi, Vandals, Alans and Visigoths in Hispania after their invasion of 409.

hou-junji.s: Hou Junji was a Tang dynasty general who served the emperor Taizong. He led campaigns against the Tuyuhun and in 640 conquered the oasis kingdom of Gaochang near Turpan, which became the Tang prefecture of Xizhou.

hintsa-kakhawuta.s: Hintsa kaKhawuta was king of the Gcaleka Xhosa, paramount among the Xhosa chiefs, from about 1820 to 1835. During the Sixth Frontier War the British accused him of harbouring cattle taken from the Cape Colony, and he came to the camp of Governor Benjamin D'Urban to negotiate.

hofuf.s: Hofuf is the main city of the al-Ahsa oasis in the Eastern Province of Saudi Arabia, one of the largest palm oases in the world. It was the seat of the Ottoman province of Lahsa from the 16th century and of the Banu Khalid emirate in the 17th and 18th centuries.

heo-hwang-ok.s: Heo Hwang-ok is the legendary queen of King Suro, founder of Geumgwan Gaya in Korea. The Samguk yusa says she arrived by sea in 48 CE from a distant land called Ayuta, which many in modern times identify with Ayodhya in India.

hassan-ibn-thabit.s: Hassan ibn Thabit was an Arab poet of the Khazraj tribe of Medina. Before Islam he praised the Ghassanid kings of Syria, and after his conversion he became the leading poet of the Prophet Muhammad, defending him and the Muslims in verse against their opponents.

hernando-pizarro.s: Hernando Pizarro was a Spanish conquistador, the only legitimate brother of Francisco Pizarro, and a leader in the conquest of the Inca Empire. He held Cusco during Manco Inca's siege of 1536–1537, defeated Diego de Almagro at the Battle of Las Salinas in 1538 and had him…

honoratus-maynier.s: Honoratus Maynier was an official of the Dutch East India Company who served as landdrost of Graaff-Reinet, on the eastern frontier of the Cape Colony, in the 1790s. His efforts to make peace with the Xhosa and to protect Khoikhoi servants from abuse angered the frontier…

hilandar.s: Hilandar is a Serbian Orthodox monastery on Mount Athos in northern Greece, founded in 1198 by Stefan Nemanja, then the monk Simeon, and his son Sava. Richly endowed by Serbian rulers, it became the leading centre of Serbian religious life and literature in the Middle Ages and…

horea.s: Horea, born Vasile Ursu Nicola, was a Romanian serf who led the peasant revolt of 1784 in the Apuseni Mountains of Transylvania together with Cloșca and Crișan. The rebels rose against labour dues and Hungarian landlords, attacking manors across the region.

hooge.s: Hooge was a Manchu prince of the Qing dynasty, the eldest son of Hong Taiji, and held the title Prince Su. He commanded Qing armies in the conquest of China and in 1646 led the campaign into Sichuan, where Zhang Xianzhong, ruler of the Great Xi regime, was killed in early 1647.

hurricane-ivan.s: Hurricane Ivan was a powerful Atlantic hurricane that struck the Caribbean and the United States in September 2004. On 7 September it passed over Grenada, damaging or destroying about 90 per cent of the island's buildings and killing dozens of people, then went on to hit…

hawaiian-organic-act.s: The Hawaiian Organic Act was a law of the United States Congress, passed in April 1900, that established the Territory of Hawaii after the annexation of 1898. It granted US citizenship to citizens of the former Republic of Hawaii and created an elected territorial legislature,…

himalayas.s: The Himalayas are the highest mountain range on Earth, stretching about 2,400 kilometres from northern Pakistan through India, Nepal and Bhutan, between the Tibetan Plateau and the plains of the Indian subcontinent. They contain Mount Everest and many of the world's highest…

habr-yunis.s: The Habr Yunis are a major clan of the Isaaq clan family of the Somali people, living mainly in the Togdheer and Sahil regions of Somaliland and in the Somali Region of Ethiopia. Around 1787 they formed their own sultanate, breaking away from the Isaaq Sultanate, and in the…

hadiyya-language.s: Hadiyya is a Highland East Cushitic language spoken by the Hadiya people of southern Ethiopia, south-west of Addis Ababa, by more than a million people. It takes its name from the medieval Hadiya Sultanate, whose people lived in the same broad region.

highland-east-cushitic-languages.s: The Highland East Cushitic languages are a branch of the Cushitic family spoken in the highlands of southern Ethiopia, in and around the Rift Valley. The largest is Sidamo, and the group also includes Hadiyya, Kambaata, Gedeo and Alaba.

hama.s: Hama is a city on the Orontes river in western Syria, famous for its great wooden water wheels, the norias. As Hamath it was the capital of an Iron Age kingdom until Sargon II annexed it in 720 BCE, and in the Middle Ages it was ruled by a branch of the Ayyubid dynasty,…

hodna-mountains.s: The Hodna Mountains are a range in north-central Algeria, rising north of the Hodna basin and its salt lake, the Chott el Hodna. In the early 11th century the Hammadid ruler Hammad ibn Buluggin built his fortified capital, Qal'at Beni Hammad, on their slopes, north-east of the…

hansetag.s: The Hansetag, or Hanseatic Diet, was the general assembly of the Hanseatic League, attended by envoys of the member towns. The first is usually dated to 1356 at Lübeck, which hosted most later meetings.

han-shantong.s: Han Shantong was a Chinese leader of the White Lotus sect from Hebei who preached the imminent coming of the Buddha Maitreya and claimed descent from the Song emperors. In 1351 he and Liu Futong planned an uprising against the Yuan dynasty, but the plot was discovered and he…

hasanlu-lovers.s: The Hasanlu Lovers are two human skeletons found in 1972 at Hasanlu Tepe in north-western Iran, lying together in an apparent embrace in a bin where they died when the citadel was destroyed around 800 BCE. They were excavated by the University of Pennsylvania Museum's team…

hussein-of-jordan.s: Hussein of Jordan (Hussein bin Talal) was King of Jordan from 1952, when his father Talal was deposed, until his death in 1999, assuming his full powers in 1953. He lost the West Bank and East Jerusalem to Israel in 1967, expelled the Palestinian armed groups in 1970–71 and…

hyrcanus-ii.s: Hyrcanus II was a Hasmonean high priest and ruler of Judaea, the elder son of Alexander Jannaeus and Salome Alexandra. Ousted by his brother Aristobulus II, he was restored as high priest by Pompey in 63 BCE, with the Idumaean Antipater as his chief minister.

hebat.s: Hebat was a mother goddess of the Hurrians, worshipped as the consort of the storm god Teshub, especially in northern Syria and Kizzuwatna. Her cult centres included Aleppo and Kummanni, and the Hittites came to identify her with the sun goddess of Arinna.

hatay-province.s: Hatay is the southernmost province of Turkey, on the Mediterranean coast bordering Syria, with its capital at Antakya, ancient Antioch. As the Sanjak of Alexandretta it was part of French-mandated Syria until it became the autonomous Hatay State in 1938 and was annexed by…

hattic-language.s: Hattic was the language of the Hattians of central Anatolia in the 3rd and early 2nd millennium BCE. It is unrelated to the Indo-European Hittite language and to the Semitic languages and has no known relatives.

hausa-bakwai.s: The Hausa Bakwai are the seven 'true' Hausa states of tradition: Daura, Kano, Katsina, Zazzau, Gobir, Rano and Biram, said to descend from the legendary hero Bayajidda and his offspring. They are contrasted with the Banza Bakwai, seven 'illegitimate' states.

hammam-ibn-yusuf.s: Hammam ibn Yusuf was the leader of the Hawwara, the Arab tribal confederation that dominated Upper Egypt under Ottoman rule in the mid-18th century. From Farshut he controlled much of the Nile valley from Asyut to Aswan as a tax farmer.

hecatomnus.s: Hecatomnus was a Carian dynast from Mylasa who became satrap of Caria for the Achaemenid Empire around 392 BCE, founding the Hecatomnid dynasty. He ruled from Mylasa and was succeeded in turn by his children Mausolus, Artemisia II, Idrieus, Ada and Pixodarus, who made Caria a…

hamar.s: Hamar is a town in eastern Norway on the shore of Lake Mjøsa, the administrative centre of Innlandet county. It became the seat of a bishop in 1152 and grew around its cathedral, whose ruins are now protected under a glass shelter.

hrorek.s: Hrørek was a petty king of Hedmark in eastern Norway in the early 11th century, according to the sagas of Snorri Sturluson. He joined a revolt of the Uppland kings against Olaf Haraldsson around 1018, was captured and blinded, and was later sent away to Iceland, where saga…

helian-bobo.s: Helian Bobo was the founder of the Xia state, one of the Sixteen Kingdoms of northern China, and was of Tiefu Xiongnu origin. Born Liu Bobo, he broke away from Later Qin in 407 and proclaimed himself Heavenly King of Great Xia.

hydra-greece.s: Hydra is a Greek island in the Saronic Gulf, off the eastern coast of the Peloponnese. In the 18th century its shipowners built a large merchant fleet, and during the Greek War of Independence from 1821 Hydriot ships formed the core of the Greek navy.

herodium.s: Herodium is a fortified palace built by Herod the Great on an artificially heightened, cone-shaped hill south of Bethlehem, in the West Bank. Herod chose it as his burial place, and in 2007 archaeologists led by Ehud Netzer identified what they believed to be his tomb on its…

hikone.s: Hikone is a city in Shiga Prefecture, Japan, on the eastern shore of Lake Biwa. It grew around Hikone Castle, built by the Ii clan between 1603 and 1622, whose original keep is one of five in Japan designated National Treasures.

harima-province.s: Harima Province was an old province of Japan on the Inland Sea, now the south-western part of Hyōgo Prefecture. After the Battle of Sekigahara it was given to Ikeda Terumasa, who rebuilt Himeji Castle, the province's main stronghold.

hyogo-prefecture.s: Hyōgo Prefecture is a prefecture of the Kansai region of Japan, reaching from the Inland Sea to the Sea of Japan, with its capital at Kobe. It was formed in the 1870s from parts of the old provinces of Settsu, Harima, Tajima, Tamba and Awaji.

haouz.s: The Haouz is a plain in central Morocco around Marrakesh, between the High Atlas and the Jebilet hills, irrigated by streams from the mountains. It has long formed the agricultural hinterland of Marrakesh and gives its name to the modern Al Haouz province, which was the centre…

habar-gidir.s: The Habar Gidir are a Somali clan of the Hawiye clan family, belonging to its Hiraab branch and living mainly in central Somalia, in the Mudug and Galguduud regions. With the Abgaal they formed the Hiraab Imamate after the fall of the Ajuran.

hawiye.s: The Hawiye are one of the major Somali clan families, living mainly in central and southern Somalia, including Mogadishu, and in parts of Ethiopia and Kenya. They are divided into many clans, among them the Abgaal and Habar Gidir.

hiroshima-bay.s: Hiroshima Bay is an inlet of the Seto Inland Sea on the coast of Hiroshima Prefecture, Japan, sheltered by islands including Itsukushima (Miyajima). Its shallow waters have supported oyster farming for centuries, and the city of Hiroshima grew at its head on the delta of the…

hiroshima-prefecture.s: Hiroshima Prefecture is a prefecture in the Chūgoku region of western Honshu, Japan, on the Inland Sea, with its capital at Hiroshima. It was formed in 1871 from the Hiroshima domain of the Asano and covers the old provinces of Aki and Bingo.

homun.s: Homún is a town in the Mexican state of Yucatán, south-east of Mérida. Before the Spanish conquest it was one of the Maya towns of the province of Hocabá, governed by a local batab under the provincial ruler.

hussain-hotak.s: Hussain Hotak was the last ruler of the Hotak dynasty, a younger son of Mirwais Hotak, who governed Kandahar from 1725. After the Afghans were driven out of Persia he held the city as an independent ruler.

hatun-xauxa.s: Hatun Xauxa was an Inca provincial centre in the Mantaro valley of central Peru, near the modern town of Jauja. Built on the main Inca road after the conquest of the Xauxa and Huanca peoples, it held storehouses, a plaza and administrative buildings.

hatunmarca.s: Hatunmarca was a fortified hilltop town of the Xauxa people in the Yanamarca valley, a side valley of the Mantaro in central Peru. Flourishing from the 14th century until the Inca conquest, it was the largest settlement of the Yanamarca valley, with thousands of circular…

huastec-people.s: The Huastec, or Teenek, are an Indigenous people of north-eastern Mexico who speak a Mayan language that separated from the other Mayan languages long ago. They live in the Huasteca region of northern Veracruz and San Luis Potosí.

huastec-adolescent.s: The Huastec Adolescent is a limestone statue of a young man, made by the Huastec people of north-eastern Mexico in the Postclassic period and found at Tamuín, San Luis Potosí. The naked figure, carrying a child on its back and covered with incised designs, is often identified…

huasteca.s: The Huasteca is a region on the Gulf coast of Mexico, covering parts of Veracruz, San Luis Potosí, Tamaulipas, Hidalgo, Querétaro and Puebla. Named after the Huastec people, its fertile lowlands produced cotton and textiles, and from the 15th century much of it paid tribute to…

hungarian-working-peoples-party.s: The Hungarian Working People's Party was the ruling communist party of Hungary from 1948 to 1956, formed by the forced merger of the Communist Party with the Social Democrats. Led by Mátyás Rákosi, it imposed a Stalinist dictatorship.

hungarian-democratic-forum.s: The Hungarian Democratic Forum was a centre-right political party founded in 1987 at Lakitelek by intellectuals opposed to communist rule. It won Hungary's first free elections in 1990, and its leader József Antall became prime minister.

huronia.s: Huronia, or Wendake, was the homeland of the Wendat (Huron) Confederacy between Georgian Bay and Lake Simcoe in present-day Ontario, Canada. In the early 17th century it held some 20,000 to 30,000 people in palisaded villages, and it was the centre of French Jesuit missions.

hutsuls.s: The Hutsuls are a Ukrainian-speaking highland people of the eastern Carpathians, in south-western Ukraine and northern Romania. Traditionally herders, woodcutters and rafters, they are known for their wooden churches, embroidery, woodcarving and music.

house-of-burgh.s: The House of Burgh was an Anglo-Norman family that acquired vast lands in Ireland after the invasion of the 12th century. William de Burgh founded the line, and his descendants became lords of Connacht and earls of Ulster.

hawwara.s: The Hawwara are a Berber tribal confederation, originally of Tripolitania in present-day Libya. In the 8th century they supported Ibadi Kharijite imams there, and branches spread across North Africa and to al-Andalus, where the Banu Razin of Albarracín claimed Hawwara origin.

henry-king-of-portugal.s: Henry was a son of King Manuel I who became a cardinal and inquisitor general before succeeding his great-nephew Sebastian as king of Portugal in 1578. Elderly and celibate, he could not provide an heir, and his short reign was taken up by the succession question.

himmatnagar.s: Himmatnagar is a town in northern Gujarat, India, headquarters of Sabarkantha district, on the Hathmati river. Founded in the 15th century as Ahmednagar by Sultan Ahmad Shah I of Gujarat, it became the capital of Idar State and was renamed after Maharaja Himmat Singh in the…

hispano-moroccan-war-1859-1860.s: The Hispano-Moroccan War was fought between Spain and Morocco from October 1859 to April 1860, after attacks on the Spanish enclave of Ceuta. A Spanish army under Leopoldo O'Donnell took Tetouan in February 1860 and won at Wad Ras in March.

hildesheim.s: Hildesheim is a city in Lower Saxony, Germany, south-east of Hanover. Louis the Pious founded its bishopric in 815, and under Bishop Bernward around 1000 it became a centre of Ottonian art; its cathedral and St. Michael's Church are a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

hathumod.s: Hathumod was the first abbess of Gandersheim, a daughter of the Saxon count Liudolf and his wife Oda. She led the community from its foundation at Brunshausen in 852 and its move to Gandersheim in 856 until her death in an epidemic in 874.

hrotsvitha-of-gandersheim.s: Hrotsvitha of Gandersheim was a canoness of Gandersheim Abbey in Saxony and a Latin writer, regarded as the first known woman poet of Germany and the first known dramatist of the Latin West since antiquity. Writing around 960, she composed six plays modelled on those of…

herford.s: Herford is a town in eastern Westphalia, in the German state of North Rhine-Westphalia, north-east of Bielefeld. It grew around Herford Abbey, a community of noble women founded around 789, whose abbesses ruled as princesses of the Empire, and the town itself became a member…

hortulus.s: Hortulus, or On the Cultivation of Gardens, is a Latin poem written around 840 by Walafrid Strabo, abbot of Reichenau on Lake Constance. It describes the labour of the gardener and some two dozen plants of a monastery garden, with their uses in medicine and their symbolic…

hirsau-abbey.s: Hirsau Abbey was a Benedictine monastery in the northern Black Forest, Germany, founded in the 9th century and refounded in 1065. Under Abbot William of Hirsau from 1069 it adopted the customs of Cluny and became the centre of the Hirsau reform, which spread to more than a…

hiawatha.s: Hiawatha is a co-founder of the Iroquois Confederacy in Haudenosaunee tradition, an Onondaga or Mohawk leader who became the spokesman of the Great Peacemaker. Grieving for his murdered family, he was consoled by the Peacemaker with wampum, and together they won the five…

hargeisa.s: Hargeisa is the capital and largest city of Somaliland, the self-declared republic in north-western Somalia. It grew as a trading town and became the capital of British Somaliland in 1941.

hezb-e-islami.s: Hezb-e Islami is an Afghan Islamist party founded in the 1970s and led by Gulbuddin Hekmatyar. It was one of the strongest mujahideen parties fighting the Soviet Union and the communist government, favoured by Pakistan's intelligence service.

hezb-e-wahdat.s: Hezb-e Wahdat is an Afghan political party founded in 1989 as a union of Shia factions representing the Hazara people, under Abdul Ali Mazari. During the civil war of the 1990s it fought other factions for control of western Kabul.

house-of-keys.s: The House of Keys is the elected lower house of Tynwald, the parliament of the Isle of Man, with 24 members. It claims descent from the assembly of the Norse kingdom of Mann and the Isles, making Tynwald one of the oldest continuous parliaments in the world.

hibernia.s: Hibernia is the classical Latin name for Ireland, related to Greek forms such as Ierne and Ptolemy's Iouernia, which derive from the same Celtic root as the Irish name Ériu. The Romans never conquered Ireland, though they traded with it, and the name was used in Latin texts…

halmahera.s: Halmahera is the largest island of the Maluku Islands in eastern Indonesia, an irregular, four-armed island in the province of North Maluku. The small clove-producing islands of Ternate and Tidore lie off its west coast, and the sultanates of Ternate, Tidore and Jailolo…

haveli.s: A haveli is a traditional townhouse or mansion of the Indian subcontinent, built around one or more inner courtyards. Wealthy merchant families, especially in Rajasthan and Gujarat, decorated their havelis with carved stone or wooden facades, balconies and wall paintings.

hirde-shah.s: Hirde Shah was a son of the Bundela ruler Chhatrasal and became Raja of Panna in central India on his father's death in 1731. Chhatrasal's lands were divided among his sons and his Maratha ally Baji Rao I: Hirde Shah received Panna, while his brother Jagat Raj took Jaitpur and…

hussain-tekri.s: Hussain Tekri is a Muslim shrine at Jaora in the Ratlam district of Madhya Pradesh, India, built in the late 19th century by a Nawab of Jaora and dedicated to the memory of Husayn ibn Ali. It draws large numbers of pilgrims of all faiths, especially during Muharram, many…

husain-shah-sharqi.s: Husain Shah Sharqi was the last sultan of Jaunpur, ruling from 1458 to 1479. He enlarged the kingdom and completed the Jama Masjid of Jaunpur, but his repeated campaigns to seize Delhi from Bahlul Lodi failed.

huining-prefecture.s: Huining Prefecture, later called Shangjing, the Upper Capital, was the first capital of the Jurchen Jin dynasty, near modern Harbin in Heilongjiang, China. Wanyan Aguda ruled from there after proclaiming the dynasty in 1115.

huining-monk.s: Huining was a Chinese Buddhist monk from Sichuan who sailed to the Javanese kingdom of Heling, known as Kalingga, in 664 or 665. There he worked with the local scholar Jnanabhadra to translate a Buddhist scripture on the Buddha's final nirvana into Chinese.

hanwant-singh.s: Hanwant Singh was the last ruling Maharaja of Jodhpur, succeeding in 1947. At independence he briefly considered acceding to Pakistan before signing the accession to India, and in 1949 his state merged into Rajasthan.

hussein-shah-of-johor.s: Hussein Shah was a Malay prince recognised by the British as Sultan of Johor in 1819, when Stamford Raffles needed a ruler to sanction a British post at Singapore. Passed over in the succession, he signed the treaty that let the East India Company settle there, and in 1824…

hangul.s: Hangul is the Korean alphabet, created in 1443 under King Sejong of Joseon and promulgated in 1446 as the Hunminjeongeum, "the proper sounds for instructing the people". Its letters represent consonants and vowels and are grouped into syllable blocks.

homs.s: Homs, ancient Emesa, is a city in western Syria on the Orontes river, commanding the Homs gap between the coast and the inland plains. In Roman times it was ruled by the Emesene dynasty and was the home of the sun god Elagabal, and in the Middle Ages it was the seat of Ayyubid…

hokuriku-region.s: The Hokuriku region lies on the Sea of Japan coast of central Honshu, covering the prefectures of Niigata, Toyama, Ishikawa and Fukui. Known for heavy winter snow and rich rice farming, it was a stronghold of the True Pure Land school of Buddhism, whose leagues, the Ikko-ikki,…

hujung-galuh.s: Hujung Galuh was a port on the lower Brantas River in East Java, mentioned in inscriptions of King Airlangga in the 11th century. Airlangga built dams on the Brantas to protect it from floods, and it served as a harbour where ships from other islands and overseas traded.

hanamkonda.s: Hanamkonda is a town in Telangana, India, now part of the Warangal urban area. It was the early seat of the Kakatiya dynasty before the capital moved to nearby Orugallu, or Warangal, in the late 12th century.

haihaya.s: The Haihayas were an ancient clan of Indian tradition, described in the Puranas and the Mahabharata as a branch of the Yadus ruling from Mahishmati on the Narmada. Their most famous legendary king, Kartavirya Arjuna, was slain by Parashurama.

haakon-vi-of-norway.s: Haakon VI was king of Norway from 1343 to 1380 and also king of Sweden from 1362 to 1364. He married Margaret, daughter of Valdemar IV of Denmark, in 1363, and their son Olaf inherited both Denmark and Norway.

hojo-clan.s: The Hōjō clan was a Japanese warrior family that controlled the Kamakura shogunate as hereditary regents (shikken) from the early 13th century, ruling through puppet shoguns. They defeated the retired emperor Go-Toba in 1221, issued the Goseibai Shikimoku law code and led…

hojo-tokimune.s: Hōjō Tokimune was the eighth regent (shikken) of the Kamakura shogunate, ruling Japan from 1268 to 1284. He rejected Kublai Khan's demands for submission and led the defence against the Mongol invasions of 1274 and 1281, both repelled with the help of storms.

honen.s: Hōnen was a Japanese Buddhist monk who founded the Jōdo-shū, the Pure Land school, in 1175. He taught that salvation came through calling on the name of the Buddha Amida (the nembutsu) rather than through difficult practices, opening Buddhism to ordinary people.

hami.s: Hami, or Kumul, is an oasis city in eastern Xinjiang, China, at the eastern end of the Tarim Basin routes and the gateway from Gansu. After the Yuan dynasty it was ruled by Chagatayid princes, then by the Kumul Khanate under Qing protection until 1930.

hatuniye-madrasa.s: The Hatuniye Madrasa is a theological college in Karaman, central Anatolia, completed in 1382. It was founded by Nefise Sultan, a daughter of the Ottoman sultan Murad I and wife of the Karamanid ruler Alaeddin Bey.

haci-ilbey.s: Hacı İlbey was a 14th-century Turkish commander from the beylik of Karesi who entered Ottoman service after its annexation. He took part in the early Ottoman conquests in Thrace under Süleyman Pasha and Murad I.

harisimhadeva.s: Harisimhadeva was the last king of the Karnat dynasty of Mithila in northern Bihar. He sponsored the codification of Maithil Brahmin genealogies in the panji registers, and his minister Jyotirishvara Thakur wrote the Varna Ratnakara.

hadejia.s: Hadejia is a town in Jigawa State in northern Nigeria, on the Hadejia River. An old Hausa town, it was taken by Fulani leaders around 1808 during the jihad of Usman dan Fodio and became the seat of the Hadejia Emirate.

hyderabad.s: Hyderabad is a city on the Musi River in the Deccan, now the capital of the Indian state of Telangana. It was founded around 1591 by Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah of Golconda, who built the Charminar, and from 1763 it was the capital of the Nizams of Hyderabad.

hyderabad-sindh.s: Hyderabad is a city on the Indus in Sindh, Pakistan. The Kalhora ruler Ghulam Shah founded it in 1768 on the site of an older fortified town, and it became the capital of the Talpur mirs of Sindh.

hajji-davud.s: Hajji Davud was a Lezgin leader from Mushkur in northern Shirvan who led a Sunni revolt against Safavid rule in the early 1720s. With Surkhay Khan of Kazikumukh he sacked Shamakhi in 1721, killing Russian merchants, which Peter the Great used as a pretext for his Persian…

harry-thuku.s: Harry Thuku was a Kenyan political leader, one of the first to organise African protest against colonial rule. In 1921 he founded the Young Kikuyu Association and campaigned against forced labour, the pass system and land loss.

husuni-kubwa.s: Husuni Kubwa is the ruin of a large palace on the island of Kilwa Kisiwani in southern Tanzania, built in the early 14th century by Sultan al-Hasan ibn Sulaiman of the Mahdali dynasty. With more than a hundred rooms, courtyards, an octagonal pool and an audience court, it was…

hudud-al-alam.s: The Hudud al-Alam, 'The Limits of the World', is an anonymous Persian geography completed in 982 and dedicated to the Farighunid amir Abu'l-Harith Muhammad of Guzgan. It describes the countries and peoples of the known world region by region.

hinda-dynasty.s: The Hinda dynasty, or Bahinda, was a royal clan that ruled several kingdoms of the African Great Lakes region, including Ankole in Uganda and Karagwe, Ihangiro, Kyamutwara and Kianja among the Haya states of north-western Tanzania. Its traditions trace it to Ruhinda, said to…

hill-of-ward.s: The Hill of Ward, anciently Tlachtga, is a hill near Athboy in County Meath, Ireland, crowned by a ringfort with multiple banks. In early Irish tradition it was the site of a great fire festival at Samhain, and in the Middle Ages it was a place of royal assemblies.

hun-manet.s: Hun Manet is a Cambodian army officer and politician, the eldest son of Hun Sen, who became prime minister of Cambodia in August 2023. A graduate of the United States Military Academy at West Point, he rose to command the Royal Cambodian Army before succeeding his father, who…

herod-archelaus.s: Herod Archelaus was a son of Herod the Great who ruled Judea, Samaria and Idumaea as ethnarch from 4 BCE to 6 CE, after Augustus denied him the royal title. His harsh rule provoked complaints from both Judeans and Samaritans, and Augustus deposed him and exiled him to Vienne…

hyspaosines.s: Hyspaosines was the founder of the kingdom of Characene at the head of the Persian Gulf. A Seleucid governor of Iranian origin, he restored the flooded city of Alexandria on the Tigris as Charax Spasinou, declared independence as Seleucid power collapsed around 141 BCE, and…

houegbadja.s: Houegbadja was king of Dahomey, in present-day Benin, probably from about 1645 to 1685, and is regarded as the true founder of the kingdom. He made Abomey its capital, built the first royal palace there and is credited with laying down many of the kingdom's institutions and…

hyfaidd-ap-bleddri.s: Hyfaidd ap Bleddri was king of Dyfed in south-west Wales in the later 9th century. Asser records that he oppressed the church of St Davids and that he submitted to Alfred the Great of Wessex in the 880s to protect himself against the sons of Rhodri the Great of Gwynedd.

historia-brittonum.s: The Historia Brittonum is a Latin history of the Britons compiled in Wales around 829–830 and traditionally attributed to Nennius. It combines legend, genealogy and annals, and contains the earliest account of Arthur's twelve battles together with stories of Vortigern, Hengist…

hung-e-azhdar.s: Hung-e Azhdar is a rock relief near Izeh in Khuzestan, south-western Iran, carved in the Parthian period. It shows a horseman, usually taken to be a Parthian king, together with standing figures including a local ruler of Elymais, and is among the main monuments of the…

house-of-valois.s: The House of Valois was a branch of the Capetian dynasty that ruled France from 1328, when Philip VI succeeded the last direct Capetian, until 1589. It led France through the Hundred Years' War and the Italian Wars, and its junior lines included the Valois dukes of Burgundy.

hailu-tekle-haymanot.s: Hailu Tekle Haymanot was an Ethiopian nobleman, son of King Tekle Haymanot of Gojjam, who governed Gojjam with the title Ras and became one of the richest lords of the empire. In 1932 Haile Selassie arrested him for helping the deposed emperor Lij Iyasu escape, and he lost his…

house-of-mortimer.s: The Mortimers were an Anglo-Norman baronial family whose lords held Wigmore Castle in the Welsh Marches from the late 11th century and built up a great lordship along the middle border. Roger Mortimer, 1st Earl of March, deposed Edward II with Queen Isabella in 1327, and…

harlech.s: Harlech is a small town on Cardigan Bay in Gwynedd, north-west Wales, in the old district of Ardudwy. Edward I built Harlech Castle there between 1283 and 1289 after his conquest of Wales.

hadramautic-language.s: Hadramautic was one of the Ancient South Arabian languages, written in the Kingdom of Hadramawt in what is now eastern Yemen from the early first millennium BCE until about the 4th century CE. It used the South Arabian (Musnad) script and is known from inscriptions at Shabwa,…

hermopolis.s: Hermopolis, ancient Egyptian Khemenu and modern el-Ashmunein, was a city in Middle Egypt and the chief cult centre of Thoth, god of wisdom and writing. Its priests taught a creation myth of eight primordial gods, the Ogdoad.

huahine.s: Huahine is an island in the Leeward group of the Society Islands in French Polynesia, made up of two parts, Huahine Nui and Huahine Iti, joined by a narrow channel. Settled by Polynesians perhaps a thousand years ago, it has one of the largest concentrations of marae in the…

haya-people.s: The Haya are a Bantu-speaking people of the Kagera region in north-western Tanzania, on the western shore of Lake Victoria. For several centuries before colonial rule they were organised in small kingdoms such as Kiziba, Kyamutwara and Ihangiro, ruled by royal clans with…

house-of-gurieli.s: The Gurieli were the ruling house of Guria, in south-western Georgia, a branch of the Vardanisdze family who governed it as eristavis of the Georgian kingdom from the 14th century and as independent princes after its break-up in the 15th. Often at war with Imereti, Mingrelia…

house-of-stuart.s: The House of Stuart was a royal dynasty that ruled Scotland from 1371 and, from the accession of James VI and I in 1603, England and Ireland as well. Its reigns saw the Plantation of Ulster, the civil wars and the execution of Charles I in 1649, the Restoration and the…

hosea.s: Hosea was a Hebrew prophet in the northern Kingdom of Israel in the 8th century BCE, during its last decades before the Assyrian conquest. The biblical Book of Hosea uses his marriage to an unfaithful wife as an image of Israel's unfaithfulness to its God, condemning the…

hathigumpha-inscription.s: The Hathigumpha inscription is a long Prakrit inscription in Brahmi script carved in the 'Elephant Cave' on Udayagiri hill near Bhubaneswar, probably in the 1st century BCE. It records year by year the deeds of Kharavela, king of Kalinga of the Mahameghavahana dynasty,…

huanggang.s: Huanggang is a city in eastern Hubei province, China, on the north bank of the Yangtze. Its area was the site of Zhu, capital of Wu Rui's Kingdom of Hengshan after 206 BCE.

hanuman-dhoka.s: Hanuman Dhoka is the old royal palace complex on Kathmandu Durbar Square in Nepal, named after a stone image of the god Hanuman that Pratap Malla set up at its gate in 1672. It was the seat of the Malla kings of Kantipur and, after 1768, of the Shah kings of Nepal until the…

hengist-and-horsa.s: Hengist and Horsa are legendary brothers said to have led the first Germanic settlers, Jutes, to Britain in the 5th century. According to Bede and the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle, they came around 449 as mercenaries of the British ruler Vortigern and then rebelled against him; Horsa…

hemis-monastery.s: Hemis Monastery is the largest and wealthiest Buddhist monastery in Ladakh, India, about 40 km south-east of Leh. It belongs to the Drukpa lineage and was founded in the 17th century under the patronage of King Sengge Namgyal.

henry-ii-lord-of-mecklenburg.s: Henry II, called the Lion, was lord of Mecklenburg in the early 14th century. A warlike prince, he fought the Hanseatic towns and his neighbours and, after the Rostock line died out in 1314, secured the lordship of Rostock against Danish claims by 1323.

hill-of-tara.s: The Hill of Tara is a low ridge in County Meath, Ireland, with prehistoric monuments including a passage tomb and earthworks. In early medieval Ireland it was the symbolic seat of the most prestigious kingship, and the title king of Tara, claimed especially by the Uí Néill,…

hegra.s: Hegra, also known as Mada'in Salih or al-Hijr, is an archaeological site near al-Ula in north-western Saudi Arabia. It was the second city of the Nabataean Kingdom after Petra, and its more than 100 monumental tombs, cut into sandstone outcrops in the 1st century BCE and 1st…

haghpat-monastery.s: Haghpat Monastery is a medieval Armenian monastery in the Lori region of northern Armenia. Queen Khosrovanuysh, wife of King Ashot III, founded it around 976, and it flourished under the Kiurikian kings of Lori as a centre of learning with a large scriptorium.

hmong-people.s: The Hmong are an ethnic group of the mountains of southern China, northern Vietnam, Laos and Thailand, speaking Hmongic languages. Many migrated south from China in the 18th and 19th centuries and settled in the highlands of northern Laos, where they grew rice and opium.

haliacmon.s: The Haliacmon, modern Aliakmonas, is the longest river flowing entirely within Greece, about 300 kilometres long. It rises in the Pindus mountains near the Albanian border and crosses western and central Macedonia to the Thermaic Gulf west of Thessaloniki.

haryanka-dynasty.s: The Haryanka dynasty ruled the Kingdom of Magadha in the Ganges valley in the 6th and 5th centuries BCE, according to Buddhist and Jain sources. Bimbisara and his son Ajatashatru, contemporaries of the Buddha and Mahavira, expanded the kingdom by conquest and marriage, and…

hill-of-uisneach.s: The Hill of Uisneach is a low hill in County Westmeath, traditionally regarded as the sacred centre of Ireland, where the ancient provinces met. Excavations have found ritual and royal structures from prehistory into the early Middle Ages, and it was associated with the…

heinrich-schliemann.s: Heinrich Schliemann was a German businessman and pioneering archaeologist who set out to prove the historical basis of Homer's epics. From 1871 he excavated Hisarlik in Turkey, identifying it as Troy, and in 1876 he found the shaft graves of Mycenae with their gold masks.

house-of-braganza.s: The House of Braganza was the royal dynasty of Portugal from 1640 to 1910 and of Brazil from 1822 to 1889. Descended from an illegitimate son of John I, the dukes of Braganza became the greatest nobles of Portugal, and in 1640 Duke John led the revolt against Spanish rule and…

heinrich-friedrich-karl-vom-stein.s: Heinrich Friedrich Karl vom und zum Stein was a Prussian statesman who, as chief minister in 1807–08, began the reforms that rebuilt Prussia after its defeat by Napoleon. His October Edict of 1807 abolished hereditary serfdom, and his municipal ordinance of 1808 introduced…

hera.s: Hera was the queen of the Greek gods, wife and sister of Zeus, and goddess of marriage and women. Her name appears on Linear B tablets from Pylos, and her great sanctuaries at Samos and Argos were among the oldest in Greece; colonists built major temples to her at Paestum…

hutu.s: The Hutu are the largest population group of Rwanda and Burundi, sharing the Kinyarwanda and Kirundi languages and much of their culture with the Tutsi and Twa. In the precolonial kingdoms the distinction was partly social, separating mostly farming Hutu from a Tutsi elite…

hanzhong.s: Hanzhong is a city in south-western Shaanxi, China, in the basin of the upper Han River between the Qinling and Daba mountains. In 206 BCE Xiang Yu made Liu Bang King of Han there, and from it Liu Bang broke out to found the Han dynasty, which took its name from the region.

hebrides.s: The Hebrides are the islands off the west coast of Scotland, divided into the Inner Hebrides, such as Skye, Mull and Islay, and the Outer Hebrides, such as Lewis and Harris. Settled by Norse from the 9th century, they belonged to the Kingdom of the Isles under Norwegian…

hms-bounty.s: HMS Bounty was a Royal Navy ship sent under William Bligh to collect breadfruit plants on Tahiti. In April 1789 part of the crew, led by Fletcher Christian, mutinied and set Bligh adrift; some mutineers settled on Pitcairn Island, while others stayed on Tahiti, where they…

hassan-ibn-al-numan.s: Hassan ibn al-Nu'man was an Arab general of the Umayyad Caliphate who completed the conquest of North Africa. He took Carthage in 695 and, after the Byzantines briefly recovered it, again in 698, and he fought the Berber queen Dihya, who defeated him before being killed around…

husaby.s: Husaby is a village and early church site in Västergötland, south-western Sweden, near Lake Vänern. Tradition holds that King Olof Skötkonung was baptised at a spring there in the early 11th century by the English missionary Sigfrid, and Husaby is regarded as one of the…

hygelac.s: Hygelac is the king of the Geats in the Old English poem Beowulf, the hero's uncle and lord. The poem describes his death on a raid into Frisia, an event that matches Gregory of Tours' account of a Scandinavian king, Chlochilaicus, killed by the Frankish prince Theudebert in…

hereford.s: Hereford is a cathedral city on the River Wye in western England, the county town of Herefordshire. A bishopric was established there in the late 7th century for the Magonsaete, and the diocese long kept the outline of their kingdom.

hermeric.s: Hermeric was king of the Suebi who led his people across the Rhine in 406 and into Hispania in 409. In 411 they received lands in Gallaecia, where he founded the Suebic kingdom with its centre at Bracara Augusta.

herminafrid.s: Herminafrid was the last king of the Thuringians, who married Amalaberga, niece of Theodoric the Great. After Theodoric's death the Frankish kings Theuderic I and Chlothar I defeated him on the Unstrut in 531 and annexed his kingdom.

haldi.s: Haldi was the chief god of Urartu, a warrior deity at the head of a pantheon that also included the storm god Teisheba and the sun god Shivini. Urartian kings attributed their victories to him and opened their inscriptions with his name.

haffon.s: Haffon, also written Huffon, was the last independent king of Whydah, or Hueda, on the coast of present-day Benin, reigning from 1708. His kingdom prospered from the Atlantic slave trade through its port, where several European companies kept forts.

halfdan-ragnarsson.s: Halfdan Ragnarsson was a Viking leader of the Great Heathen Army that invaded England in 865, later described as a son of Ragnar Lodbrok. With his brother Ivar he took York in 866–867, and he campaigned in Mercia, Wessex and against the Picts and Strathclyde.

hajo.s: Hajo is a town in the Kamrup district of Assam, India, on the north bank of the Brahmaputra, north-west of Guwahati. It was the seat of the Koch Hajo kingdom from 1581.

hayagriva-madhava-temple.s: The Hayagriva Madhava Temple is a Hindu temple on the Monikut hill at Hajo in Assam, India, dedicated to Vishnu in his horse-headed form, Hayagriva. The present stone temple was rebuilt in 1583 by the Koch king Raghudev Narayan.

hsinbyushin.s: Hsinbyushin was the third king of the Konbaung dynasty of Burma, ruling from 1763 to 1776, a son of the dynasty's founder Alaungpaya. His armies besieged and sacked the Siamese capital Ayutthaya in 1767, ending the Ayutthaya Kingdom.

hippocrates.s: Hippocrates was a Greek physician from the island of Kos, born around 460 BCE, who is traditionally called the father of medicine. He taught that diseases had natural causes rather than divine ones, and a large body of medical writings, the Hippocratic Corpus, was attributed…

hiraga-gennai.s: Hiraga Gennai was a Japanese scholar of Western learning, inventor, writer and painter of the Edo period, born in Sanuki province. He built an electrostatic generator, promoted mining and natural history, and wrote popular fiction and plays.

higo-province.s: Higo Province was an old province of Japan in central Kyushu, corresponding to modern Kumamoto Prefecture. Katō Kiyomasa received its northern half in 1588 and the whole province after the Battle of Sekigahara in 1600, and from 1632 it was held by the Hosokawa clan as the…

himachal-pradesh.s: Himachal Pradesh is a mountainous state of northern India in the western Himalaya, with its capital at Shimla. It was created in 1948 as a union of some thirty princely hill states, including Chamba, Mandi and Sirmur, absorbed the hill districts of Punjab in 1966 and became a…

haapsalu.s: Haapsalu is a seaside town in western Estonia and the capital of Lääne County, known in German as Hapsal. From the 13th century it was a residence of the bishops of Ösel-Wiek, whose castle and cathedral still stand, and it later passed to Denmark, Sweden and Russia.

hiiumaa.s: Hiiumaa is the second-largest island of Estonia, lying in the Baltic Sea north of Saaremaa, and known in German and Swedish as Dagö. Conquered by German crusaders in the 13th century, it belonged to the Bishopric of Ösel-Wiek, then to Sweden and from 1710 to Russia, and had a…

hebron.s: Hebron is a city in the southern West Bank, in the Judaean hills about 30 kilometres south of Jerusalem. It is revered by Jews, Christians and Muslims as the burial place of Abraham and the patriarchs at the Cave of the Patriarchs, enclosed by a Herodian wall.

halvad.s: Halvad is a town in Morbi district, Gujarat, India, in the Jhalawad region of northern Saurashtra near the Little Rann of Kutch. Founded in the late 15th century as the seat of the Jhala Rajputs, it remained their capital until the court moved to Dhrangadhra in the 18th…

hakodate.s: Hakodate is a port city in southern Hokkaido, Japan, on the Tsugaru Strait. It was one of the first Japanese ports opened to foreign ships under the treaties of the 1850s, and the star-shaped fort of Goryokaku was built there in the 1860s.

hastinapura.s: Hastinapura is an ancient town in Meerut district, Uttar Pradesh, India, near an old bed of the Ganges, celebrated in the Mahabharata as the capital of the Kuru kings. Excavations in the 1950s found Painted Grey Ware settlement of the early 1st millennium BCE and evidence of a…

harbin.s: Harbin is the capital of Heilongjiang province in north-east China, on the Songhua River. It grew from a small settlement after 1898, when Russia made it the headquarters of the Chinese Eastern Railway, and became a cosmopolitan city with a large Russian population.

heinrich-von-kleist.s: Heinrich von Kleist was a German dramatist, poet and short-story writer from a Prussian military family. His plays include the comedy The Broken Jug, Penthesilea and The Prince of Homburg, and his novellas include Michael Kohlhaas and The Marquise of O. Little recognised in…

hercules-kassel.s: The Hercules in Kassel is a monumental statue of Hercules standing on an octagonal pyramid and castle-like structure at the top of the Bergpark Wilhelmshöhe. Built for Landgrave Charles of Hesse-Kassel to designs by Giovanni Francesco Guerniero from 1701, it is the landmark of…

habsburg-laufenburg.s: Habsburg-Laufenburg was a junior line of the House of Habsburg, founded when the Habsburg lands were divided between brothers around 1232. Its counts held Laufenburg on the Upper Rhine, the landgraviate of the Klettgau and, for a time, Rapperswil.

house-of-schwarzenberg.s: The House of Schwarzenberg is a Franconian noble family that rose in the service of the Habsburgs and became princes of the Holy Roman Empire in 1670. It acquired large estates in Bohemia, including Český Krumlov and Hluboká, and gained the Klettgau by marriage in 1687.

hojo-ujinao.s: Hōjō Ujinao was the fifth and last head of the Later Hojo clan of Odawara in Japan. With his father Ujimasa he refused to submit to Toyotomi Hideyoshi, who besieged Odawara in 1590.

hojo-ujitsuna.s: Hōjō Ujitsuna was the second head of the Later Hojo clan of Japan, son of Hojo Soun. He adopted the surname Hojo, recalling the regents of the Kamakura shogunate, and expanded the family's lands from Sagami into Musashi, taking Edo castle in 1524.

hetu-ala.s: Hetu Ala was the walled settlement in Xinbin, Liaoning province, China, where Nurhaci proclaimed the Later Jin khanate in 1616. It served as his first capital before he moved his court to Liaoyang in 1621 and then to Shenyang.

hoan-kiem-lake.s: Hoàn Kiếm Lake, the 'Lake of the Returned Sword', is a lake in the centre of Hanoi, Vietnam. According to legend, after defeating the Ming, Lê Lợi returned his magic sword to a golden turtle that rose from the lake.

hunac-ceel.s: Hunac Ceel is a figure of Maya tradition recorded in the Books of Chilam Balam as the founder of the Cocom rule at Mayapan in northern Yucatán. According to the chronicles he survived being thrown into the sacred cenote at Chichen Itza, proclaimed a prophecy and later brought…

hezbollah.s: Hezbollah is a Lebanese Shia Islamist political party and armed group founded in 1982 with Iranian support, in response to the Israeli invasion of Lebanon. It fought Israel in southern Lebanon until the Israeli withdrawal in 2000 and in the wars of 2006 and 2024, and it also…

horace.s: Horace, Quintus Horatius Flaccus, was a leading Roman poet of the age of Augustus. The son of a freedman from Venusia, he fought for Brutus at Philippi and later won the patronage of Maecenas.

huaca-pucllana.s: Huaca Pucllana is a large adobe and clay pyramid of the Lima culture in the Miraflores district of Lima, Peru, built between about 200 and 700 CE. Its walls are made of small handmade adobe bricks set upright like books on a shelf, a technique thought to help resist earthquakes.

huaca-san-marcos.s: Huaca San Marcos is one of the largest mounds of the Maranga complex in Lima, Peru, built by the Lima culture in the first centuries CE. It stands beside the main campus of the National University of San Marcos, from which it takes its name.

h-rider-haggard.s: Sir H. Rider Haggard was an English novelist who served in the colonial administration of Natal and the Transvaal in the 1870s. His adventure novels set in Africa, above all King Solomon's Mines (1885) and She (1887), were best-sellers that shaped Victorian images of the…

house-of-haro.s: The House of Haro was a Castilian noble family that ruled the Lordship of Biscay from the 11th to the 14th century. Descended from Íñigo López Ezquerra and named after the town of Haro in La Rioja, its members, many called López de Haro, were among the most powerful magnates…

holy-grail.s: The Holy Grail is a vessel of medieval legend, identified with the cup used by Christ at the Last Supper or the dish that caught his blood at the Crucifixion. It first appears in Chrétien de Troyes's romance Perceval around 1190 and became central to Arthurian literature.

hugh-montgomery-1st-viscount-montgomery.s: Hugh Montgomery, 1st Viscount Montgomery, was a Scottish laird from Ayrshire who in 1605, with James Hamilton, acquired most of the lands of Con O'Neill of Clandeboye in north Down. He settled Scottish colonists at Newtownards, Donaghadee and Comber, laying the foundations of…

helena-dragas.s: Helena Dragaš was a Serbian noblewoman, daughter of Konstantin Dragaš, who in 1392 married the Byzantine emperor Manuel II Palaiologos. She was the mother of the last two Byzantine emperors, John VIII and Constantine XI, who used the surname Dragases after her family.

helena-of-adiabene.s: Helena was queen of Adiabene in northern Mesopotamia in the 1st century CE, wife of King Monobazus I and mother of Izates II. According to Josephus she and her son converted to Judaism.

house-of-clare.s: The Clares were an Anglo-Norman noble family named after Clare in Suffolk, among the wealthiest in medieval England. They became earls of Hertford and Gloucester, held the marcher lordship of Glamorgan from 1217 and built Caerphilly Castle, while a branch led the invasion of…

haifa.s: Haifa is a port city in northern Israel on the Bay of Haifa, at the foot of Mount Carmel. A small town in the Middle Ages, it was captured by the crusaders in 1100 and became a minor lordship of the Kingdom of Jerusalem.

house-of-berthout.s: The Berthouts were a powerful noble family of the Duchy of Brabant, lords of Grimbergen and later advocates and lords of Mechelen. From the 12th to the 14th century they contested control of Mechelen with the prince-bishops of Liège, to whom the town nominally belonged, and…

house-of-sforza.s: The Sforza were an Italian family of condottieri who ruled the Duchy of Milan from 1450 to 1535, with interruptions. Founded by Muzio Attendolo, called Sforza, the dynasty rose when his son Francesco Sforza married the last Visconti heiress and became duke.

helvis-of-ramla.s: Helvis of Ramla was the heiress of the lordship of Ramla in the Kingdom of Jerusalem, daughter of Baldwin of Ramla. Her marriage to Barisan of Ibelin brought Ramla to the Ibelin family, and their sons Hugh, Baldwin and Balian became leading barons of the kingdom.

house-of-ibelin.s: The Ibelins were a noble family of the crusader states, named after the castle of Ibelin granted to Barisan of Ibelin around 1141. Through marriage they gained Ramla, Beirut, Jaffa and Arsuf, and leaders such as Balian of Ibelin and John of Ibelin, the Old Lord of Beirut,…

henry-borwin-ii-lord-of-mecklenburg.n: Henry Borwin II, Lord of Mecklenburg
henry-borwin-ii-lord-of-mecklenburg.s: Henry Borwin II was a lord of Mecklenburg of the native Obotrite dynasty, ruling jointly with his father Henry Borwin I in the early 13th century, when German settlers and new towns transformed the region. He died in 1226, before his father, and in 1229 his lands were divided…

humphrey-iv-of-toron.s: Humphrey IV of Toron was a baron of the Kingdom of Jerusalem, stepson of Raynald of Châtillon and heir of Toron and Oultrejordain. He married Isabella, half-sister of King Baldwin IV, in 1183, but in 1186 refused to be crowned by the barons opposed to Guy of Lusignan and…

hartenstein-saxony.s: Hartenstein is a small town on the Zwickauer Mulde in western Saxony, Germany, at the edge of the Ore Mountains. Its lordship, with Hartenstein Castle and the nearby Burg Stein, was bought by the Schönburg family in 1406 and held by them under Saxon overlordship.

house-of-schonburg.s: The Schönburgs are a German noble family of imperial ministerials from the Saale region near Naumburg, first recorded in the 12th century. They built up lordships along the Zwickauer Mulde around Glauchau, Waldenburg, Lichtenstein and Hartenstein, which they held under Saxon…

hussites.s: The Hussites were followers of the Czech reformer Jan Hus, burned for heresy at Constance in 1415. Demanding communion in both kinds and reform of the Church, they rose in Bohemia and under Jan Žižka and Prokop the Great defeated a series of crusades against them in the…

harpagus.s: Harpagus was a Median noble who, according to Herodotus, saved the infant Cyrus from death ordered by King Astyages and later helped Cyrus overthrow him around 550 BCE. As Cyrus' general he conquered the Greek cities of Ionia, Caria and Lycia after the fall of Lydia, around…

hunan.s: Hunan is a province of south-central China, lying mostly south of Lake Dongting along the Xiang river, with its capital at Changsha. In the Warring States period it formed part of the state of Chu, and in the 10th century it was the seat of the independent kingdom of Ma Chu.

hili-archaeological-park.s: Hili is an archaeological area near Al Ain in the United Arab Emirates, part of the UNESCO World Heritage Site of the Cultural Sites of Al Ain. Its best-known monument is the Hili Grand Tomb, a round stone tomb of the Umm an-Nar period (about 2500–2000 BCE) decorated with…

hajar-mountains.s: The Hajar Mountains are the highest range of eastern Arabia, running some 700 km through northern Oman and the eastern United Arab Emirates, with Jebel Shams, about 3,000 metres high, as their highest peak. Their ophiolite rocks contain copper that was mined from the 3rd…

hadibu.s: Hadibu, formerly Tamrida, is the main town of the island of Socotra, Yemen, on its north coast. It was a seat of the Mahra sultans of Qishn and Socotra, who ruled the island from the 15th century until 1967.

harda-district.s: Harda is a district in the Indian state of Madhya Pradesh, south of the Narmada river, with its headquarters at the town of Harda. It was separated from Hoshangabad (now Narmadapuram) district in 1998.

harold-macmichael.s: Sir Harold MacMichael was a British colonial administrator who served in Sudan, as governor of Tanganyika and, from 1938 to 1944, as High Commissioner for Palestine. In 1945 he was sent to Malaya to obtain the signatures of the Malay rulers to treaties transferring their…

hindola-mahal.s: The Hindola Mahal ('swinging palace') is an audience hall at Mandu in Madhya Pradesh, India, built by the sultans of Malwa in the 15th century. Its massive sloping side walls give the impression that the building is swaying.

histadrut.s: The Histadrut, the General Federation of Labour, was founded in Haifa in 1920 as the trade union of Jewish workers in Mandatory Palestine. Under leaders such as David Ben-Gurion it also ran its own enterprises, including the construction firm Solel Boneh, a bank and a health…

heiligenkreuz-abbey.s: Heiligenkreuz Abbey is a Cistercian monastery in the Vienna Woods, Lower Austria, founded in 1133 by Margrave Leopold III of Austria. It is the oldest continuously inhabited Cistercian monastery in the world and holds the tombs of several Babenberg rulers.

hermann-ii-margrave-of-baden.s: Hermann II was a member of the house of Zähringen and the first to call himself Margrave of Baden, in 1112, after the castle of Hohenbaden above Baden-Baden. Son of Hermann I, he inherited the margravial title and lands in the Breisgau and northern Black Forest, and his…

hermann-iv-margrave-of-baden.s: Hermann IV was Margrave of Baden from 1160 until his death in 1190, a supporter of Emperor Frederick Barbarossa in his Italian wars. Before he left on the Third Crusade, his lands were divided, his son Henry receiving the castle of Hachberg and founding the Hachberg line.

hochburg.s: The Hochburg, or Hachberg Castle, is a large castle ruin near Emmendingen in the Breisgau, Baden-Württemberg. It was the seat of the margraves of Hachberg from around 1200 and was later expanded into a fortress by the margraves of Baden.

herrnhut.s: Herrnhut is a small town in Upper Lusatia, Saxony, founded in 1722 by Protestant refugees from Moravia on the estate of Count Nikolaus Ludwig von Zinzendorf. It became the centre of the renewed Moravian Church, whose missionaries spread worldwide.

hasdrubal-the-fair.s: Hasdrubal the Fair was a Carthaginian general, son-in-law of Hamilcar Barca, who succeeded him as commander in Iberia in about 229 BCE. He extended Carthaginian power by diplomacy, founded Qart Hadasht (Carthago Nova) around 227 BCE, and in 226 BCE agreed with Rome to treat…

hasdrubal-barca.s: Hasdrubal Barca was a Carthaginian general, son of Hamilcar Barca and brother of Hannibal. He commanded in Iberia during the Second Punic War, where the Scipio brothers defeated him near Hibera in 215 BCE.

hasdrubal-gisco.s: Hasdrubal Gisco was a Carthaginian general of the Second Punic War who fought the Romans in Iberia until Scipio defeated him at Ilipa in 206 BCE. He won King Syphax of the Masaesyli for Carthage by marrying him to his daughter Sophonisba.

harvard-university.s: Harvard University, founded as Harvard College in 1636 by vote of the General Court of the Massachusetts Bay Colony, is the oldest institution of higher learning in the United States. It was named after the clergyman John Harvard, who left it his library and half his estate in…

hamdullahi.s: Hamdullahi, the House of Praise, was the capital of the Massina Empire in the inner Niger delta of present-day Mali. It was founded around 1820 by Seku Amadu after his jihad against the Fulbe chiefs and their Bambara overlords, and was laid out as a planned Islamic city with a…

hilla.s: Hilla, or al-Hilla, is a city in central Iraq on a branch of the Euphrates, near the ruins of Babylon. It was founded around 1101 by the Mazyadid emir Sadaqa ibn Mansur as the capital of his Arab principality and soon became a leading centre of Shia scholarship, home to…

helisson.s: The Helisson is a river of Arcadia in the central Peloponnese, Greece, a tributary of the Alpheus. Megalopolis, the capital of the Arcadian League founded between 371 and 368 BCE, was built on both of its banks, with the theatre and federal assembly hall on the south side and…

hyblon.s: Hyblon was a king of the Sicels in eastern Sicily in the eighth century BCE. According to Thucydides, he gave land to settlers from Megara in Greece who had failed to settle elsewhere, and they founded the city of Megara Hyblaea, named partly after him, around 728 BCE on the…

hoelun.s: Hö'elün was the mother of Temüjin, later Genghis Khan. According to the Secret History of the Mongols, she was seized by Yesügei from her Merkit husband, and after Yesügei's death she raised her children in poverty when their clan abandoned them.

hutelutush-inshushinak.s: Hutelutush-Inshushinak was a king of Elam in the late 12th century BCE, the last important ruler of the Shutrukid dynasty of the Middle Elamite period. Around 1110 BCE he was defeated by Nebuchadnezzar I of Babylon, who invaded Elam and brought back the statue of the god…

hawara.s: Hawara is an archaeological site at the entrance to the Faiyum in Egypt, where Amenemhat III of the Twelfth Dynasty built his mud-brick pyramid in the 19th century BCE. Next to it stood his vast mortuary temple, which Greek writers such as Herodotus described as the Labyrinth,…
