habuba-kabira.s: Habuba Kabira is an archaeological site on the middle Euphrates in northern Syria, now flooded by Lake Assad behind the Tabqa Dam. Excavated in the late 1960s and 1970s, it revealed a planned, walled town of the late fourth millennium BCE with southern Mesopotamian…

harihara-ii.s: Harihara II was emperor of Vijayanagara of the Sangama dynasty from 1377 to 1404, the son of Bukka I. He consolidated the empire's hold on southern India, extending its control along the west coast and over the Tamil lands, and fought the Bahmani Sultanate for the Raichur Doab.

huitong-canal.s: The Huitong Canal was a section of the Grand Canal cut through western Shandong under the Yuan dynasty and opened in 1289. Running northwards towards Linqing, it formed part of the direct route that allowed grain from southern China to reach the northern capital by water.

heraios.s: Heraios was a ruler in Bactria known only from his coins, which were inscribed in Greek and show him in Hellenistic royal style with a steppe-style portrait. He probably reigned in the late 1st century BCE or early 1st century CE and was one of the Yuezhi lords; his coins call…

haji-ebrahim-khan-kalantar.s: Haji Ebrahim Khan Kalantar was the kalantar (mayor) of Shiraz who in 1791 betrayed the last Zand ruler, Lotf Ali Khan, and handed the city to Agha Mohammad Khan Qajar. He became the first grand vizier of the Qajar dynasty and kept the post under Fath-Ali Shah, until the shah,…

hamu-kanzibe.s: Hamu kaNzibe was a Zulu prince, a son of King Mpande and a powerful chief in northern Zululand. A rival of his half-brother Cetshwayo, he defected to the British during the Anglo-Zulu War of 1879 and was made one of the thirteen appointed chiefs in Wolseley's settlement.

henry-francis-fynn.s: Henry Francis Fynn was an English trader and adventurer who arrived at Port Natal in 1824 with Francis Farewell's party and spent years at the courts of Shaka and Dingane. His diary, edited and published in 1950, is one of the main eyewitness sources for the early Zulu…

hvar.s: Hvar is a Croatian island in the central Adriatic. Greeks from Paros founded the colony of Pharos there in 384 BCE, and the Stari Grad Plain preserves their field divisions as a World Heritage Site.

hamilcar-i-of-carthage.s: Hamilcar was a Carthaginian general of the Magonid family who commanded the great expedition to Sicily in 480 BCE. Landing at Panormus, he besieged the Greek city of Himera but was defeated by Gelon of Syracuse and Theron of Akragas at the Battle of Himera, where he was killed…

hikayat-patani.s: The Hikayat Patani is a Malay chronicle of the sultanate of Pattani on the east coast of the Malay Peninsula, probably compiled in the 17th and 18th centuries. It tells of the founding of the kingdom, the conversion of its ruler Phaya Tu Nakpa to Islam as Sultan Ismail Shah…

hypogeum-of-the-volumni.s: The Hypogeum of the Volumni is an Etruscan chamber tomb near Perugia, discovered in 1840. Cut into the rock in the shape of a house, it belonged to the Velimna family, known in Latin as the Volumni, and held finely carved cinerary urns, the most famous being that of Arnth…

hellenion.s: The Hellenion was a sanctuary at Naukratis in the Nile Delta, built jointly by Greek cities trading in Egypt under the pharaoh Amasis II in the 6th century BCE. Herodotus names nine founders: Chios, Teos, Phocaea, Clazomenae, Rhodes, Cnidus, Halicarnassus, Phaselis and Mytilene.

hukbalahap.s: The Hukbalahap was a communist-led guerrilla army of peasants in central Luzon, Philippines, founded in 1942 to fight the Japanese occupation. After the war its fighters, denied recognition and pressed by landlords, rose against the government of the new Philippine republic.

hamid-ii-of-pontianak.s: Hamid II was the last reigning sultan of Pontianak in West Kalimantan, Indonesia, from 1945. He led West Kalimantan within the federal United States of Indonesia, served as a minister of state and led the design of the national emblem, the Garuda Pancasila.

hubal.s: Hubal was a god worshipped in pre-Islamic Mecca, whose statue of red stone with a golden hand stood inside the Kaaba. Divination arrows were cast before it to settle disputes and decisions.

hoffmann-von-fallersleben.s: August Heinrich Hoffmann von Fallersleben was a German poet and scholar of early German literature. In 1841, on Heligoland, he wrote the 'Lied der Deutschen', whose third stanza is the national anthem of Germany.

hoxter.s: Höxter is a town on the Weser in eastern North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany. It grew up beside the abbey of Corvey, founded nearby in 822, whose abbots claimed lordship over it, and it was a member of the Hanseatic League.

hrabanus-maurus.s: Hrabanus Maurus was a Frankish monk, scholar and theologian, a pupil of Alcuin. As master of the school and then abbot of Fulda from 822 to 842 he made it one of the leading centres of learning in the Carolingian world, earning the title 'teacher of Germany'.

hildegard-of-the-vinzgau.s: Hildegard was a Frankish queen from the Alemannian nobility who married Charlemagne around 771 and bore him nine children, among them Louis the Pious. She was a patron of churches, including the abbey of Kempten, which honoured her as its benefactress.

hallein.s: Hallein is a town on the Salzach in the Austrian state of Salzburg, south of the city of Salzburg. Its salt mine on the Dürrnberg, already worked by the Celts in the Iron Age, was the main source of the prince-archbishops' wealth.

hortus-eystettensis.s: The Hortus Eystettensis is a celebrated botanical book published in 1613, recording the plants of the garden laid out by Prince-Bishop Johann Conrad von Gemmingen at the Willibaldsburg in Eichstätt. Compiled by the apothecary Basilius Besler, it has 367 copperplate engravings…

halberstadt.s: Halberstadt is a town north of the Harz in Saxony-Anhalt, Germany. Made a bishopric around 804 under Charlemagne, it was ruled by prince-bishops until the Peace of Westphalia gave it to Brandenburg in 1648.

havelberg.s: Havelberg is a small town on the Havel near its junction with the Elbe in Saxony-Anhalt, Germany. Otto I founded a bishopric there around 948 to convert the Slavs, and it was restored after the Wendish Crusade of 1147; its Romanesque cathedral was consecrated in 1170.

hildesheim-diocesan-feud.s: The Hildesheim Diocesan Feud was a war from 1519 to 1523 between Bishop John IV of Hildesheim, allied with the Duke of Lüneburg, and the Guelph dukes of Brunswick-Wolfenbüttel and Calenberg. Although the bishop's side won at Soltau in 1519, Emperor Charles V backed the dukes,…

house-of-petrovic-njegos.s: The House of Petrović-Njegoš ruled Montenegro from 1696 to 1918, first as prince-bishops passing the office from uncle to nephew and, from 1852, as secular princes. Nikola I took the title of king in 1910.

house-of-shervashidze.s: The Shervashidze, called Chachba in Abkhaz, were the princely family that ruled Abkhazia from the late Middle Ages until 1864. Originally governors under the Georgian kings and the Dadiani of Mingrelia, they became independent princes as Georgia broke up, and many converted to…

harzgerode.s: Harzgerode is a small town in the eastern Harz mountains of Saxony-Anhalt, Germany. Nearby, in the Selke valley, stand the ruins of Anhalt castle, which gave its name to the principality of Anhalt.

house-of-bourbon-conde.s: The House of Bourbon-Condé was a branch of the French royal house of Bourbon, founded by Louis I de Bourbon, Prince of Condé, a Protestant leader in the Wars of Religion who died in 1569. Its members held the title of Prince of Condé and were among the greatest nobles of…

house-of-gramont.s: The House of Gramont is a French noble family from the Basque borderland of Lower Navarre, holding the castle and principality of Bidache. Its members served as governors of Navarre and Béarn and as soldiers and courtiers of the French kings.

henrichemont.s: Henrichemont is a small town in the Cher department of central France. It was founded in 1608 by Maximilien de Béthune, Duke of Sully, as the capital of his sovereign principality of Boisbelle, and named after his king, Henry IV.

house-of-bourbon-montpensier.s: The House of Bourbon-Montpensier was a branch of the French house of Bourbon that held Montpensier in Auvergne. Its most famous member, Charles III, Constable of Bourbon, rebelled against Francis I and lost his lands in 1523.

hann-munden.s: Hann. Münden is a town in southern Lower Saxony, Germany, where the Werra and Fulda rivers meet to form the Weser.

herzberg-am-harz.s: Herzberg am Harz is a town on the south-western edge of the Harz in Lower Saxony, Germany. Its hilltop castle served as a residence of the Guelph dukes of Grubenhagen until their line died out in 1596, after which it passed to the Lüneburg and Hanoverian branches.

heitersheim.s: Heitersheim is a small town in the Markgräflerland of Baden-Württemberg, south-west of Freiburg im Breisgau. The Knights Hospitaller held it from the 13th century, and from 1505 it was the seat of their Grand Prior of Germany, who ruled it as a small principality of the Empire…

house-of-hasan-jalalyan.s: The Hasan-Jalalyans were an Armenian princely family of Khachen in Artsakh, descended from Hasan-Jalal Dawla, who ruled in the 13th century. After his execution by the Mongols in 1261 the family survived as local lords, and under the Safavids they held the melikdom of Khachen.

hulbuk.s: Hulbuk is the site of a medieval city in southern Tajikistan, at Kurbonshahid near Vose, identified as the capital of the principality of Khuttal. Its citadel and palace, excavated from the mid-20th century, flourished in the 9th to 12th centuries under the local rulers of…

haardt.s: The Haardt is the eastern edge of the Palatinate Forest in Rhineland-Palatinate, Germany, a range of wooded hills rising steeply above the Upper Rhine Plain. Its sunny lower slopes carry the vineyards of the German Wine Route, and its spurs are crowned with medieval castles…

hans-adam-ii-prince-of-liechtenstein.s: Hans-Adam II has been reigning Prince of Liechtenstein since 1989. Trained in business, he restructured the princely family's finances and art collections before his accession.

house-of-grimaldi.s: The House of Grimaldi is a family of Genoese origin that has ruled Monaco since 1297, when François Grimaldi seized its fortress. One of the great Guelph clans of Genoa, the family lost and regained Monaco several times before securing it in the 15th century, and from 1612 its…

honore-ii-prince-of-monaco.s: Honoré II was the first ruler of Monaco to style himself prince, from 1612. By the Treaty of Péronne of 1641 he placed Monaco under French protection and expelled its Spanish garrison, receiving the duchy of Valentinois in France in return.

hadamar.s: Hadamar is a small town in Hesse, Germany, near Limburg an der Lahn. From 1607 to 1711 it was the seat of the counts, later princes, of Nassau-Hadamar, whose baroque palace survives.

house-of-orleans-longueville.s: The Orléans-Longueville were a French noble family descended from Jean de Dunois, the Bastard of Orléans and companion of Joan of Arc. Dukes of Longueville from 1505, they acquired the County of Neuchâtel by marriage in 1504 and ruled it until the line died out with Marie de…

hlukhiv.s: Hlukhiv is a town in Sumy Oblast in north-eastern Ukraine. First mentioned in 1152 in the Chernigov lands, it was the seat of a small principality of the Olgovichi, from which the princes of Novosil and the Upper Oka descended.

house-of-bernadotte.s: The House of Bernadotte is the royal house of Sweden, founded by the French marshal Jean-Baptiste Bernadotte, who was elected Swedish crown prince in 1810 and became king as Charles XIV John in 1818. Its kings also ruled Norway in personal union until 1905.

heinrich-lxxii-prince-reuss-of-lobenstei.n: Heinrich LXXII, Prince Reuss of Lobenstein and Ebersdorf
heinrich-lxxii-prince-reuss-of-lobenstei.s: Heinrich LXXII, Prince Reuss of Lobenstein and Ebersdorf, ruled the small Thuringian principality of Reuss-Ebersdorf from 1822 and inherited Lobenstein in 1824. He governed as an old-fashioned absolutist and was known for his eccentric, petty decrees.

heinrich-xxii-prince-reuss-of-greiz.n: Heinrich XXII, Prince Reuss of Greiz
heinrich-xxii-prince-reuss-of-greiz.s: Heinrich XXII, Prince Reuss of Greiz, ruled the principality of Reuss Elder Line from 1859, at first under his mother's regency. He sided with Austria in the war of 1866, after which Prussia occupied his small state, and he remained a stubborn opponent of Prussian dominance…

heidecksburg.s: The Heidecksburg is a baroque palace on a hill above Rudolstadt in Thuringia, Germany. It was the residence of the counts and princes of Schwarzburg-Rudolstadt, who rebuilt it after a fire in 1735 with grand state rooms.

house-of-eggenberg.s: The House of Eggenberg was an Austrian noble family from Graz that rose to great wealth in Habsburg service. Hans Ulrich von Eggenberg, chief adviser of Emperor Ferdinand II, was made a prince and received the Bohemian duchy of Krumau.

hluboka-nad-vltavou.s: Hluboká nad Vltavou, in German Frauenberg, is a small town on the Vltava in South Bohemia, Czech Republic. The princes of Schwarzenberg bought its castle in 1661 and in the 19th century rebuilt it in Romantic Tudor Gothic style, modelled on Windsor Castle.

henri-coiffier-de-ruze-marquis-of-cinq-m.n: Henri Coiffier de Ruzé, Marquis of Cinq-Mars
henri-coiffier-de-ruze-marquis-of-cinq-m.s: Henri Coiffier de Ruzé, Marquis of Cinq-Mars, was a favourite of Louis XIII of France. Encouraged by the king's brother Gaston of Orléans and the Duke of Bouillon, he plotted to overthrow Cardinal Richelieu and made a secret treaty with Spain.

havel.s: The Havel is a river in north-eastern Germany, about 330 kilometres long, a right tributary of the Elbe. It flows south from the Mecklenburg Lake District through Berlin-Spandau and Potsdam, then west past Brandenburg an der Havel, forming many lakes.

hermonassa.s: Hermonassa was an ancient Greek city on the Taman peninsula, on the Asian side of the Cimmerian Bosporus, founded in the 6th century BCE. It was one of the main towns of the Bosporan Kingdom, trading grain and fish with the Greek world.

herzog-august-library.s: The Herzog August Library in Wolfenbüttel, Lower Saxony, was founded in 1572 by Duke Julius of Brunswick-Wolfenbüttel and greatly enlarged by Duke Augustus the Younger, after whom it is named. By the late 17th century it was one of the largest libraries in Europe.

horus.s: Horus was an ancient Egyptian sky god, shown as a falcon or a falcon-headed man. In myth he was the son of Osiris and Isis who avenged his father against Set, and every living king was seen as Horus on earth, using a Horus name written in a serekh.

halifax-resolves.s: The Halifax Resolves were adopted by North Carolina's Fourth Provincial Congress at Halifax on 12 April 1776. They authorised the colony's delegates to the Continental Congress to vote for independence from Britain, the first such official instruction by any colony.

holdfast-bay.s: Holdfast Bay is a bay on the eastern shore of Gulf St Vincent in South Australia, now lined by the Adelaide suburbs of Glenelg and Brighton. Governor John Hindmarsh proclaimed the Province of South Australia there on 28 December 1836, a date still marked each year as…

ha-long-bay.s: Ha Long Bay is a bay in the Gulf of Tonkin in northern Vietnam, known for its thousands of limestone islands and pillars. On 5 June 1948 an agreement signed aboard a French warship in the bay recognised in principle the independence of Vietnam within the French Union,…

harshacharita.s: The Harshacharita ('Deeds of Harsha') is a Sanskrit prose biography of Harsha, king of Thanesar and Kannauj, written by his court poet Banabhatta in the 7th century. In eight chapters it tells of the poet's own life, the Pushyabhuti family, the deaths of Prabhakaravardhana and…

house-of-karen.s: The House of Karen was one of the seven great noble families of Parthian and Sasanian Iran, with lands centred on Nahavand in Media. Its members served as generals and ministers, among them Sukhra, the power behind the throne in the 480s.

hadhrami-bedouin-legion.s: The Hadhrami Bedouin Legion was a British-officered force raised in 1939 in the Eastern Aden Protectorate, modelled on the Arab Legion of Transjordan. Recruited mainly from Bedouin tribes, it kept order in the Qu'aiti and Kathiri sultanates of Hadramawt, guarding roads, wells…

helmold-of-bosau.s: Helmold of Bosau was a German priest and chronicler in Holstein. His Latin Chronicle of the Slavs describes the conversion and conquest of the Polabian and Baltic Slavs, the German settlement of their lands and the mission of his patron Bishop Vicelin, and is a main source for…

hierotheos.s: Hierotheos was a Byzantine monk consecrated bishop of 'Turkia', the land of the Hungarians, in the mid-10th century. According to the chronicler John Skylitzes, the Hungarian chief called the gyula was baptised in Constantinople around 952 and took Hierotheos home with him.

highland-clearances.s: The Highland Clearances were the eviction of large numbers of tenants from the Scottish Highlands and islands, mainly between about 1750 and 1860. Landowners removed them to make way for large sheep farms and later deer forests, often resettling them on small coastal crofts.

hermanus-van-wyk.s: Hermanus van Wyk was the first Kaptein of the Rehoboth Basters in present-day Namibia. He led the Basters out of the northern Cape Colony in 1868 and settled them at Rehoboth in 1870, and in 1885 he signed a protection treaty with Germany that preserved the community's autonomy.

hijikata-toshizo.s: Hijikata Toshizō was a Japanese swordsman and vice-commander of the Shinsengumi, the special police force that defended the shogunate in Kyoto in the 1860s. He fought on through the Boshin War and joined the Republic of Ezo in Hokkaido.

hurricane-mitch.s: Hurricane Mitch was one of the deadliest Atlantic hurricanes on record, striking Central America in late October and early November 1998. Its torrential rains caused floods and landslides that killed about 11,000 people, mostly in Honduras and Nicaragua, including some 2,000…

halabja-massacre.s: The Halabja massacre was a chemical weapons attack by Iraqi forces on the Kurdish town of Halabja on 16 March 1988, near the end of the Iran–Iraq War. Mustard gas and nerve agents killed an estimated 3,200 to 5,000 people, most of them civilians, and injured thousands more.

harper-liberia.s: Harper is a port town in south-eastern Liberia on Cape Palmas, the capital of Maryland County. It was founded in 1834 by settlers sent by the Maryland State Colonization Society and named after Robert Goodloe Harper, a supporter of the colonisation movement.

hindu-arabic-numeral-system.s: The Hindu–Arabic numeral system is the decimal place-value system of writing numbers with ten digits, including zero, used throughout the world today. It developed in India by the 6th or 7th century, was taken up by mathematicians of the Islamic world such as al-Khwarizmi, and…

hornacheros.s: The Hornacheros were Moriscos from the town of Hornachos in Extremadura, Spain, a community known for its cohesion and martial reputation. Expelled with the other Moriscos between 1609 and 1614, they settled in the kasbah of Rabat at the mouth of the Bou Regreg river in Morocco.

house-of-montefeltro.s: The House of Montefeltro was an Italian noble family that ruled Urbino and the mountainous Montefeltro district on the borders of Romagna and the Marche from the 13th century until 1508. Its members were Ghibelline captains and condottieri, and Federico da Montefeltro became…

house-of-elders-somaliland.s: The Guurti, or House of Elders, is the upper chamber of the parliament of Somaliland, made up of clan elders and their representatives. Councils of elders mediated in the conferences that ended Somaliland's internal conflicts, and the Borama conference of 1993 gave them a…

hildebrand-jost.s: Hildebrand Jost was Prince-Bishop of Sion from 1613 to 1638. In a long struggle with the communes (Zenden) of the Upper Valais over temporal power, he was forced in 1628 and finally in 1634 to renounce the Carolina, the claim that the bishops ruled the Valais by a grant of…

harald-hardrada.s: Harald Hardrada (Harald Sigurdsson) was king of Norway from 1046 to 1066. A half-brother of Olaf II, he served for years in the Byzantine Varangian Guard before returning to share and then hold the Norwegian throne.

heian-kyo.s: Heian-kyō ('capital of peace and tranquillity') was the capital of Japan founded by Emperor Kanmu in 794, on the site of modern Kyoto. Laid out on a grid modelled on the Chinese capital Chang'an, it remained the imperial seat for more than a thousand years and gave its name to…

heijo-kyo.s: Heijō-kyō was the capital of Japan from 710 to 784, on the site of modern Nara. Built on a grid plan modelled on Chang'an, the capital of Tang China, it gave its name to the Nara period, when the Buddhist temples Tōdai-ji and Kōfuku-ji were built and the ritsuryō state reached…

hizen-province.s: Hizen Province was an old province of Japan in north-western Kyushu, covering modern Saga Prefecture and most of Nagasaki Prefecture. In the 16th century it was the base of the Ryuzoji and of the Christian Arima and Omura families, and its port of Nagasaki became the centre of…

hagakure.s: Hagakure, meaning 'hidden by leaves', is a guide to the conduct of the samurai drawn from the sayings of Yamamoto Tsunetomo, a retainer of the Nabeshima lords of Saga. It was recorded by the younger samurai Tashiro Tsuramoto between 1709 and 1716.

hurricane-beryl.s: Hurricane Beryl was a powerful Atlantic hurricane of July 2024, the earliest on record to reach Category 5 strength. On 1 July it struck the southern Grenadines with winds of about 240 kilometres an hour, destroying most homes on Union Island and on Grenada's Carriacou.

heraion-of-samos.s: The Heraion of Samos was the great sanctuary of the goddess Hera on Samos, near the mouth of the Imbrasos river, where tradition placed her birth. From the 8th century BCE it had some of the earliest monumental Greek temples, and in the 6th century the Samians began a vast…

hikayat-raja-pasai.s: The Hikayat Raja Pasai is a Malay chronicle of the sultanate of Samudera Pasai in northern Sumatra, probably composed in the 14th century and among the oldest works of Malay literature. It tells of the founding of the kingdom and the conversion of its first ruler, Merah Silu,…

hasan-juri.s: Hasan Juri was a Shia Sufi preacher in Khorasan, a disciple of Shaykh Khalifa, whose followers spread a message of resistance to unjust rule and expectation of the Mahdi. After his alliance with the Sarbadar leader Wajih al-Din Mas'ud, his dervishes formed a large part of the…

hamirpur-district-uttar-pradesh.s: Hamirpur district is a district in the Bundelkhand region of Uttar Pradesh, India, lying between the Yamuna and Betwa rivers, with its headquarters at the town of Hamirpur. In the 19th and early 20th centuries it bordered several small princely states of Bundelkhand, and the…

helier-de-carteret.s: Helier de Carteret was a Jersey nobleman, Seigneur of Saint Ouen, who colonised the Channel Island of Sark. In 1565 Elizabeth I granted him the island as a fief on condition that he keep it settled with at least forty men able to defend it against pirates and the French.

hitachi-province.s: Hitachi Province was an old province of eastern Japan, corresponding to most of modern Ibaraki Prefecture, north-east of Edo. From the 12th century the Satake clan were its leading warrior house, until Tokugawa Ieyasu moved them to Akita in 1602.

hitchiti.s: The Hitchiti were a Muskogean-speaking people of the Lower Creek towns in Georgia. In the 18th century many Hitchiti-speaking towns moved into Florida, where they formed a core of the Seminole people.

hasekura-tsunenaga.s: Hasekura Tsunenaga was a samurai in the service of Date Masamune who led a Japanese embassy to Spain and Rome from 1613 to 1620. Sailing via Mexico, he met King Philip III and was received by Pope Paul V in 1615.

hemadri.s: Hemadri, also known as Hemadpant, was minister to the Seuna Yadava kings Mahadeva and Ramachandra in the 13th century. He compiled the Chaturvarga Chintamani, a great Sanskrit digest of religious law, and wrote on medicine and other subjects.

huaihai-road.s: Huaihai Road is a major shopping street in central Shanghai. Under the French Concession it was known from 1915 as the Avenue Joffre, after the French marshal, and became the main street of a fashionable residential district.

huang-jinrong.s: Huang Jinrong was a Chinese detective and gang boss who served for decades as a senior officer of the French Concession police in Shanghai while running opium, gambling and theatre businesses. A leading figure of the Green Gang, he was the patron of Du Yuesheng and helped…

hongkou.s: Hongkou is a district of Shanghai north of Suzhou Creek. An American settlement was established there in 1848 and merged with the British settlement in 1863 to form the International Settlement.

hamad-ibn-isa-al-khalifa.s: Hamad ibn Isa Al Khalifa was ruler of Bahrain from 1932 to 1942, after acting as ruler from 1923 when Britain forced his father, Isa ibn Ali, to step aside. With the adviser Charles Belgrave he introduced administrative reforms, courts and schools.

hamad-bin-khalifa-al-thani.s: Hamad bin Khalifa Al Thani was emir of Qatar from 1995, when he deposed his father Khalifa bin Hamad, until he abdicated in favour of his son Tamim in 2013. He used the country's vast natural gas revenues to transform Qatar, founded the Al Jazeera network in 1996, hosted a…

hyuga-province.s: Hyūga Province was an old province on the east coast of Kyushu, Japan, corresponding roughly to modern Miyazaki Prefecture. In the 16th century it was contested between the Itō clan, the Ōtomo and the Shimazu, who won it after defeating the Ōtomo at Mimikawa in 1578.

haytham-ibn-khalid.s: Haytham ibn Khalid was an Arab governor of Shirvan from the Yazidid family who in 861, as Abbasid authority collapsed after the murder of the caliph al-Mutawakkil, declared himself Shirvanshah. He turned the governorship into a hereditary principality with its capital at…

homma-family.s: The Homma family were rice merchants and landowners of Sakata in Dewa Province, Japan, among the richest commoner families of the Edo period. They lent heavily to the Shōnai Domain and other lords and in return received samurai status.

heliodorus-pillar.s: The Heliodorus pillar is a stone column at Besnagar near Vidisha in central India, set up around 113 BCE. Its inscription records that Heliodorus, a Greek envoy from Taxila sent by the Indo-Greek king Antialcidas, raised this Garuda pillar in honour of Vasudeva, calling…

huaca-loro.s: Huaca Loro is an adobe pyramid in the Sicán Precinct at Batán Grande on the north coast of Peru, built during the Middle Sicán period of about 900–1100. Excavations led by Izumi Shimada in the early 1990s uncovered its East Tomb, the burial of a lord with large quantities of…

homer.s: Homer is the ancient Greek poet to whom the Iliad and the Odyssey are attributed, epic poems probably composed in the 8th or 7th century BCE from a long oral tradition. The Iliad tells of the Trojan War and the Odyssey of Odysseus's return home.

hryhorii-skovoroda.s: Hryhorii Skovoroda (1722–1794) was a Ukrainian philosopher, poet and teacher, educated at the Kyiv-Mohyla Academy. After teaching at the Kharkiv Collegium he spent his last decades as a wandering thinker in Sloboda Ukraine, writing philosophical dialogues, fables and the verse…

hongguang-emperor.s: The Hongguang Emperor (1607–1646), Zhu Yousong, Prince of Fu, was the first emperor of the Southern Ming. Enthroned at Nanjing in 1644 after the Chongzhen Emperor's suicide, he presided over a court divided by factional struggles while the Qing advanced.

huchuquan.s: Huchuquan was the last effectively independent chanyu of the Southern Xiongnu, ruling from 195 to 216. In the wars at the end of the Han dynasty his people fought for and against various warlords until, in 216, Cao Cao detained him at Ye and divided the Southern Xiongnu into…

hassaniya-arabic.s: Hassaniya Arabic is the variety of Arabic spoken in Mauritania, Western Sahara, southern Morocco and parts of Algeria, Mali and Senegal. It descends from the speech of the Beni Hassan Arab tribes who moved into the western Sahara from the late Middle Ages and largely replaced…

hamad-bin-isa-al-khalifa.s: Hamad bin Isa Al Khalifa (born 1950) is the king of Bahrain. He succeeded his father, Isa bin Salman, as emir in 1999, and after a referendum on the National Action Charter proclaimed Bahrain a kingdom and himself king in 2002, restoring an elected parliament.

huaiyang-district.s: Huaiyang is a district of Zhoukou in eastern Henan province, China. It occupies the site of Wanqiu, capital of the State of Chen, and later of the city of Chen, which briefly served as the capital of Chu after 278 BCE and was the base of Chen Sheng's revolt against Qin in 209…

hubei.s: Hubei is a province of central China on the middle Yangtze, with its capital at Wuhan. In antiquity it was the heartland of the State of Chu, whose capital Ying lay near Jingzhou, and it has yielded many Chu tombs and bamboo texts.

han-fei.s: Han Fei (c. 280–233 BCE) was a prince of the State of Han and the leading theorist of Legalism. The book named after him, the Han Feizi, argues that a ruler should govern through clear laws, strict rewards and punishments and techniques for controlling officials, rather than…

huangchuan-county.s: Huangchuan County is a county in Xinyang, in south-eastern Henan province, China, on the Huai River plain. Near it lie the remains of the walled capital of the ancient State of Huang, a state of the Ying clan destroyed by Chu in 648 BCE, from which the county takes its name.

house-of-thani.s: The House of Thani is the ruling family of Qatar, descended from Thani bin Muhammad, whose son Muhammad bin Thani emerged as the leading sheikh of the Qatar peninsula in the mid-nineteenth century. Under Jassim bin Muhammad it consolidated its authority over the tribes, and…

hancheng.s: Hancheng is a county-level city in eastern Shaanxi, on the west bank of the Yellow River opposite Shanxi. It is the traditional birthplace of the historian Sima Qian, whose temple and tomb stand there, and its old town keeps many Ming and Qing buildings.

huaiyi.s: The Huaiyi were peoples of the Huai River region of present-day northern Anhui and Jiangsu, outside the Zhou royal domain. Western Zhou bronze inscriptions record repeated campaigns against them and tribute taken from them, and states such as Xu rose among them.

handan.s: Handan is a city in southern Hebei, at the foot of the Taihang Mountains. It was the capital of the State of Zhao from 386 BCE until its capture by Qin in 228 BCE, and a great commercial city of the Warring States period.

haraz-mountains.s: The Haraz Mountains are a highland region of western Yemen between Sanaa and the Red Sea coast, known for fortified villages on steep terraced slopes and for coffee growing. In 1047 the Isma'ili missionary Ali ibn Muhammad al-Sulayhi rose in revolt there and founded the…

hobyo.s: Hobyo is a port town on the Indian Ocean coast of central Somalia, in the Mudug region. It was the capital of the Sultanate of Hobyo, founded by Yusuf Ali Kenadid around 1878, which exported livestock, hides and gum until Italy annexed it in 1925.

hemu.s: Hemu was a Hindu general and minister of the Sur Empire who rose from a merchant background to command the armies of Adil Shah Suri. After winning many battles against Afghan rivals and the Mughals, he took Delhi in 1556 and proclaimed himself king as Vikramaditya.

house-of-lancaster.s: The House of Lancaster was a branch of the English royal house of Plantagenet, descended from John of Gaunt, Duke of Lancaster. It held the throne from 1399, when Henry IV deposed Richard II, through Henry V, victor of Agincourt, to Henry VI.

hayat-tahrir-al-sham.s: Hayat Tahrir al-Sham was a Sunni Islamist armed group in the Syrian civil war, formed in 2017 from the former al-Nusra Front, once al-Qaeda's Syrian branch, and other factions. Led by Abu Mohammad al-Julani (Ahmed al-Sharaa), it governed much of Idlib province.

husni-al-zaim.s: Husni al-Za'im was a Syrian army officer who led the first military coup in Syria's history in March 1949, overthrowing President Shukri al-Quwatli after the defeat in the 1948 war with Israel. He made himself president, signed an armistice with Israel and introduced some…

hammudid-dynasty.s: The Hammudids were a Berber-backed Arab dynasty of Idrisid descent that briefly held the caliphate of Córdoba between 1016 and 1027 during the civil war that broke up al-Andalus. They then ruled the Taifa of Málaga and Algeciras, claiming the caliphal title, and led an…

hisham-iii-of-cordoba.s: Hisham III (c. 975–1036) was the last Umayyad caliph of Córdoba, proclaimed in 1026 and installed in the city only in 1029 after years of civil war. His government, run by an unpopular vizier, could not restore order, and in 1031 the notables of Córdoba deposed him and…

habbus-ibn-maksan.s: Habbus ibn Maksan (died 1038) was the Zirid ruler of Granada from about 1019 and the real founder of its Berber dynasty. A nephew of Zawi ibn Ziri, he took power when his uncle returned to Ifriqiya and built Granada up as a capital.

house-of-lara.s: The House of Lara was one of the most powerful noble families of medieval Castile, named after Lara de los Infantes near Burgos. In the 12th century its members, among them Manrique Pérez de Lara, dominated the regency of the young Alfonso VIII in rivalry with the Castro…

huete.s: Huete is a town in the province of Cuenca, Castile-La Mancha, Spain. In the 11th century it was, with Uclés, a stronghold of the Berber Banu Dhi al-Nun before they took power in Toledo.

hakka-people.s: The Hakka are a Han Chinese people whose ancestors migrated in waves from northern China to the hill country of Guangdong, Fujian and Jiangxi, keeping a distinct Hakka language. Many emigrated to Taiwan and South-East Asia, where they worked as miners and farmers, notably in…

huiyuan.s: Huiyuan (334–416) was a Chinese Buddhist monk of the Eastern Jin period who founded a monastic community on Mount Lu. He corresponded with the translator Kumarajiva, argued in a famous treatise that monks need not bow to rulers, and in 402 gathered followers in a vow to be…

hierapolis-castabala.s: Hierapolis-Castabala is an ancient city in the plain of eastern Cilicia, near Osmaniye in southern Turkey. Known for its sanctuary of the goddess Perasia, it was the seat of the Tarcondimotid client kings in the 1st century BCE and later a Roman and Byzantine town.

hartapu.s: Hartapu was a great king who ruled in south-central Anatolia after the fall of the Hittite Empire, known from Luwian hieroglyphic inscriptions at Kızıldağ, Karadağ and Burunkaya. He called himself son of a great king Mursili, and an inscription found at Türkmen-Karahöyük in…

huelva.s: Huelva is a port city in Andalusia, south-western Spain, where the Odiel and Tinto rivers meet, and capital of the province of the same name. As ancient Onoba it was a major centre of the Tartessian world, where Phoenician and Greek traders obtained silver and copper from the…

hulun-lake.s: Hulun Lake is a large lake in Hulunbuir, in north-eastern Inner Mongolia, China, and one of the country's largest freshwater lakes. Fed by the Kherlen and Orshuun rivers, it lies in grasslands that were home to the medieval Tatars and other steppe peoples, and it gave the…

hame-castle.s: Häme Castle is a medieval brick and stone castle in Hämeenlinna, southern Finland. Tradition links its founding to the Swedish expedition of Birger Jarl to Tavastia around 1249, though the present building dates mainly from the late 13th and 14th centuries.

ho-chunk.s: The Ho-Chunk, also called the Winnebago, are a Siouan-speaking Native American people of the western Great Lakes, whose homeland lay in present-day Wisconsin. Some of their warriors joined Tecumseh's confederacy and fought at Tippecanoe in 1811.

hermogenes-architect.s: Hermogenes was a Greek architect of the Hellenistic period, probably from Priene or Alabanda, admired by Vitruvius as an innovator in the Ionic order. His works included the temple of Dionysus at Teos and the temple of Artemis Leukophryene at Magnesia on the Maeander, which…

hairun.s: Hairun was sultan of Ternate in the Maluku Islands from 1535 to 1570. He sought to balance alliance with the Portuguese, who held a fort on the island, against the interests of Ternate and of Islam, and was at one point taken to Goa by them.

hawaii-admission-act.s: The Hawaii Admission Act was a law of the United States Congress signed by President Dwight D. Eisenhower on 18 March 1959. It provided for the admission of the Territory of Hawaii as a state, subject to a vote of its people, who approved it by a large majority in June.

hammer-deroburt.s: Hammer DeRoburt was a Nauruan politician who led his country to independence and served as its first president. As Head Chief of the Nauruans he negotiated with Australia, Britain and New Zealand, rejecting resettlement and securing independence on 31 January 1968 and control…

hiri-motu.s: Hiri Motu is a simplified form of the Motu language of the Port Moresby area and one of the national languages of Papua New Guinea. It developed from the trading language of the hiri voyages between the Motu and the peoples of the Gulf of Papua, and spread as Police Motu under…

herodias.s: Herodias was a Herodian princess, a granddaughter of Herod the Great. She left her first husband, Herod's son Herod II, to marry his half-brother Herod Antipas, tetrarch of Galilee and Peraea, a union denounced by John the Baptist.

hadrians-villa.s: Hadrian's Villa is the vast country residence built by the Roman emperor Hadrian near Tibur, modern Tivoli, east of Rome, between about 118 and 138. Covering more than 100 hectares, it combined palaces, baths, theatres, libraries and pools inspired by buildings the emperor had…

henry-salt.s: Henry Salt was an English artist, diplomat and collector. He travelled twice in Ethiopia, in 1805 and 1809–1810, visiting Ras Wolde Selassie in Tigray on a mission for the British government, and published accounts of his journeys.

hamamatsu.s: Hamamatsu is a city in western Shizuoka Prefecture, Japan, on the Pacific coast of the former province of Totomi. Tokugawa Ieyasu moved his base there in 1570 and rebuilt its castle, holding it through his wars with Takeda Shingen until he moved to Sunpu in 1586.

hachisuka-clan.s: The Hachisuka clan was a Japanese samurai family from Owari province that rose in the service of Toyotomi Hideyoshi. In 1585 Hachisuka Iemasa received Awa province on Shikoku and built Tokushima Castle, and his son Yoshishige sided with Tokugawa Ieyasu in 1600.

hachisuka-yoshishige.s: Hachisuka Yoshishige was the first daimyo of the Tokushima domain on Shikoku. The son of Hachisuka Iemasa, he fought for Tokugawa Ieyasu in the Sekigahara campaign of 1600 while his father withdrew from public life, and was confirmed in Awa province.

hidalgo-state.s: Hidalgo is a state of central Mexico, north of Mexico City, with its capital at Pachuca. It contains the archaeological site of Tula, capital of the Toltecs in the Early Postclassic period, and the silver mines of Pachuca and Real del Monte, worked since the colonial period.

hoki-province.s: Hoki was an old province of Japan in the west of modern Tottori Prefecture, on the Sea of Japan coast, including Mount Daisen and the town of Yonago. From 1617 it formed part of the Tottori domain of the Ikeda family together with neighbouring Inaba, and it was merged into…

het-volk.s: Het Volk, 'The People', was an Afrikaner political party founded in the Transvaal in 1905 by Louis Botha and Jan Smuts to work for self-government and reconciliation with English-speaking whites after the Second Boer War. It won the first elections of the self-governing…

hippolytus-son-of-theseus.s: Hippolytus is a figure of Greek mythology, the son of Theseus and an Amazon queen. A devotee of Artemis who scorned Aphrodite, he was falsely accused by his stepmother Phaedra and died when a bull sent by Poseidon frightened his horses.

haamonga-a-maui.s: The Haʻamonga ʻa Maui is a stone trilithon on the north-eastern coast of Tongatapu, Tonga. Two upright slabs of coral limestone, about five metres high, support a lintel set into notches at their tops.

hakor.s: Hakor, called Achoris by the Greeks, was the strongest king of the Twenty-ninth Dynasty of Egypt, reigning for about thirteen years in the 390s and 380s BCE. He allied with Evagoras of Cyprus and Athens, hired Greek mercenaries under the Athenian general Chabrias and repelled…

hiram-i.s: Hiram I was king of Tyre in the 10th century BCE. According to the Bible he was an ally of David and Solomon, supplying cedar, cypress and skilled craftsmen for Solomon's temple and palace and joining Israel in trading voyages to Ophir.

hammir-singh-of-mewar.s: Hammir Singh was a ruler of Mewar in southern Rajasthan who recovered the fort of Chittor around 1326, a generation after Alauddin Khalji of the Delhi Sultanate had sacked it in 1303. He belonged to the Sisodia branch of the Guhila dynasty and took the title of rana.

holodomor.s: The Holodomor, 'killing by hunger', was the famine of 1932–1933 in Soviet Ukraine, caused by Stalin's forced collectivisation, impossible grain quotas, the blacklisting of villages and bans on peasants leaving in search of food. Estimates of the dead in Ukraine range from…

henri-van-der-noot.s: Henri van der Noot was a Brussels lawyer who led the conservative party in the Brabant Revolution of 1789 against the reforms of Emperor Joseph II in the Austrian Netherlands. From exile in Breda he organised the émigré army that invaded the country in October 1789.

house-of-david.s: The House of David was the dynasty that, according to the Hebrew Bible, descended from King David and ruled the Kingdom of Judah from Jerusalem for about four centuries, until the Babylonian conquest of 587/586 BCE. The phrase appears in the Tel Dan stele of the 9th century…

hithadhoo.s: Hithadhoo is the largest island of Addu Atoll in the southern Maldives and the administrative centre of Addu City. In 1959–1963 it served as the capital of the breakaway United Suvadive Republic under Abdullah Afeef.

huvadhu-atoll.s: Huvadhu Atoll is one of the largest atolls in the world, in the south of the Maldives, divided for administration into Gaafu Alif and Gaafu Dhaalu. In 1959 its islands joined Addu and Fuvahmulah in the United Suvadive Republic against the government in Malé, which sent forces…

harishena-vakataka.s: Harishena was the last known king of the Vatsagulma branch of the Vakataka dynasty, ruling in the late 5th century. Inscriptions claim conquests across central and southern India, and his reign was the high point of Vakataka power.

hilderic.s: Hilderic was a king of the Vandals in North Africa, a grandson of Gaiseric and, through his mother, of the Roman emperor Valentinian III. He ended the persecution of Nicene Christians and sought friendship with Constantinople.

huneric.s: Huneric was king of the Vandals in North Africa, son and successor of Gaiseric. As a young man he had been a hostage in Italy, and he married Eudocia, daughter of the emperor Valentinian III.

haute-loire.s: Haute-Loire is a department of the Massif Central in south-central France, in the Auvergne-Rhône-Alpes region, with its prefecture at Le Puy-en-Velay. Created in 1790, it covers the upper valley of the Loire and most of the old province of Velay, with parts of Auvergne and…

huy.s: Huy is a town on the Meuse in the province of Liège, Belgium. In 985 Otto III granted the county of Huy to Bishop Notger of Liège, and it became one of the principality's 'good towns'; its charter of liberties of 1066 is among the earliest urban charters in Europe.

huancavelica.s: Huancavelica is a city in the central Andes of Peru, at about 3,700 metres. Its mercury deposits, found in 1563, were worked from the 1570s with forced mita labour and supplied the mercury used to refine silver at Potosí, making it vital to the Spanish colonial economy.

hiv-aids.s: HIV/AIDS is the disease caused by the human immunodeficiency virus, which weakens the immune system and, untreated, leads to acquired immunodeficiency syndrome (AIDS). First identified in 1981, it became a global pandemic that has killed more than 40 million people, with…

harihara-i.s: Harihara I was the founder, with his brother Bukka I, of the Vijayanagara Empire and its first ruling house, the Sangama dynasty. Having probably served the Kampili or Hoysala rulers, the brothers established their kingdom on the Tungabhadra around 1336 as Delhi Sultanate…

harihara.s: Harihara is a Hindu deity combining Vishnu (Hari) and Shiva (Hara) in one figure, usually shown with one half of the body bearing Shiva's attributes and the other half Vishnu's. Popular in early medieval India, the image was especially important in pre-Angkorian Cambodia,…

hateg-country.s: The Hațeg Country is a basin in south-western Transylvania, Romania, enclosed by the Retezat and other ranges of the Southern Carpathians. A medieval Romanian district ruled by its knezes, it contains the ruins of Ulpia Traiana Sarmizegetusa, capital of Roman Dacia, and early…

huarpa-culture.s: The Huarpa culture flourished in the Ayacucho basin of the central Peruvian highlands in the first half of the 1st millennium CE. Its people farmed terraced hillsides with the help of irrigation canals and made distinctive painted pottery.

hedong-shanxi.s: Hedong, meaning "east of the river", is a historical name for the region of south-western Shanxi east of the great southward bend of the Yellow River, and in Tang and later times for most of Shanxi. It was a Qin and Han commandery, rich in salt from the lake at Yuncheng.

haojing.s: Haojing, or Hao, was the main capital of the Western Zhou dynasty, founded by King Wu on the east bank of the Feng River south-west of present-day Xi'an. With Fengjing on the opposite bank it formed the Zhou royal centre, known as Zongzhou.

hornkranz.s: Hornkranz was the fortified base of the Nama leader Hendrik Witbooi in the highlands of central Namibia, west of Rehoboth. On 12 April 1893 German colonial troops under Curt von François attacked it by surprise, killing many of its people, most of them women and children.

henan.s: Henan is a province of central China on the middle and lower Yellow River, with Zhengzhou as its capital. Often called the cradle of Chinese civilisation, it holds the Erlitou site, the Shang capitals at Zhengzhou and Anyang, and the old imperial capitals of Luoyang and Kaifeng.

hinawi.s: The Hinawi are one of the two great tribal factions of Oman, named after the Bani Hina and traditionally associated with Yemeni descent and the Ibadi imamate. Their rivalry with the Ghafiri faction, named after the Bani Ghafir, crystallised in the civil war that broke out in…

haryana.s: Haryana is a state of northern India surrounding Delhi on three sides, with Chandigarh, shared with Punjab, as its capital. The region includes Kurukshetra and Panipat, scenes of famous battles, and lay at the heart of ancient and medieval north Indian states.

huaca-mateo-salado.s: Huaca Mateo Salado is an archaeological complex in central Lima, Peru, made up of five large stepped adobe pyramids. Built by the Ychsma culture of the central coast in the Late Intermediate period and later used by the Incas, it was one of the main ceremonial centres of the…

hodeidah.s: Hodeidah is a port city on the Red Sea coast of Yemen, in the coastal plain of the Tihama, and the country's main port for imports. It grew in the 19th century under Ottoman rule, when it replaced Mocha as the chief port of the region.

hamengkubuwono-ix.s: Hamengkubuwono IX (1912–1988) was sultan of Yogyakarta from 1940 until his death and a leading figure of the Indonesian independence struggle. He supported the Republic of Indonesia from 1945, offered Yogyakarta as its capital from 1946 to 1949 and became governor of the…

haghartsin.s: Haghartsin is a medieval monastery in the forested hills near Dilijan in the Tavush province of Armenia. Its churches and refectory date mainly from the 10th to the 13th centuries, with major building under the Zakarid princes Zakare and Ivane in the early 13th century.

harichavank.s: Harichavank is a monastery in the village of Harich in the Shirak province of Armenia, near Artik. Founded in the 7th century, it was enlarged after 1201, when the Zakarid princes Zakare and Ivane acquired it and built the large Church of the Holy Mother of God.

huave.s: The Huave, who call themselves Ikoots, are an Indigenous people of the Pacific coast of the Isthmus of Tehuantepec in Oaxaca, Mexico, living around coastal lagoons where fishing is central to their way of life. Their language is an isolate, unrelated to its neighbours.

hashid.s: The Hashid are one of the two great tribal confederations of northern Yemen, alongside the Bakil, living in the highlands north of Sanaa. Long a main military support of the Zaydi imams, they are known for their cohesion, and their paramount sheikhs of the al-Ahmar family…

honaine.s: Honaine is a small port on the Mediterranean coast of western Algeria, north-west of Tlemcen. In the Middle Ages it was one of the main harbours of the Zayyanid kingdom of Tlemcen, through which goods from the Saharan caravan routes were traded with European merchants.

hua-county.s: Hua County is a county of Anyang in northern Henan, China, on the old course of the Yellow River. Its ancient city of Huatai guarded a major crossing of the river and was a strategic fortress in the wars of the Sixteen Kingdoms period: it was the capital of the Dingling state…

hengyang.s: Hengyang is a city in southern Hunan, China, on the Xiang River near the sacred Mount Heng. Known as Hengzhou in imperial times, it was where Wu Sangui proclaimed himself emperor of Zhou in 1678 during the Revolt of the Three Feudatories, and where he died months later.

hungarian-invasions-of-europe.s: The Hungarian invasions of Europe were the raids made by the Magyars from the Carpathian Basin into Germany, Italy, France and the Balkans between about 899 and 970. Mounted archers struck as far as Bremen, southern France and Constantinople.

hussite-wars.s: The Hussite Wars were fought in Bohemia from 1419 to about 1434 between the followers of the reformer Jan Hus and Catholic rulers led by Emperor Sigismund. Hussite armies under Jan Žižka and Prokop the Great, using wagon forts and firearms, defeated five crusades sent against…

herero-wars.s: The Herero Wars were the colonial wars in German South West Africa, now Namibia, in which the Herero and then the Nama rose against German rule in 1904. After the Battle of Waterberg in August 1904, General Lothar von Trotha drove the Herero into the Omaheke desert and issued…

harappa.s: Harappa is an archaeological site in Punjab, Pakistan, near a former course of the Ravi River, the remains of a major city of the Indus Valley Civilisation. Settled from about 3300 BCE, it was at its largest in the Mature Harappan phase, about 2600–1900 BCE, covering some 150…

hallstatt-culture.s: The Hallstatt culture was the main archaeological culture of western and central Europe in the early Iron Age, from about 800 to 450 BCE, and is commonly associated with speakers of Proto-Celtic. It grew out of the Urnfield culture and is named after Hallstatt in Austria,…

hochdorf-chieftains-grave.s: The Hochdorf Chieftain's Grave is a Celtic burial chamber of the Hallstatt period near Hochdorf an der Enz in Baden-Württemberg, Germany, dating from about 530 BCE. Excavated in 1978–1979, it held a man laid on a bronze couch 2.75 metres long with eight wheels, wearing a…

harriet-tubman.s: Harriet Tubman was an American abolitionist and social activist who was born into slavery in Dorchester County, Maryland. After escaping to Philadelphia in 1849, she made some thirteen missions back to rescue about seventy enslaved people, among them members of her family,…

henry-sylvester-williams.s: Henry Sylvester Williams was a Trinidadian lawyer, activist, councillor and writer, among the founders of the Pan-African movement. As a law student in London he founded the African Association in 1897 with Alice Kinloch and Thomas Josiah Thompson, and in July 1900 organised…

horse-collar.s: A horse collar is a padded harness collar that spreads a load across a horse's shoulders and chest without pressing on its windpipe; it was invented in China by the early medieval period. The earliest certain depiction is a Dunhuang cave mural of 477–499 CE, from the Northern…

hwacha.s: The hwacha was a Korean weapons platform, a wooden cart carrying a launch pad, first built in 1409 under the Joseon dynasty; it could fire up to 200 rocket-powered arrows, or volleys of arrows and bolts from gun barrels. It was developed from the juhwa and the singijeon,…

heliocentrism.s: Heliocentrism is a superseded astronomical model that placed the Sun at the centre of the universe, with the Earth and the planets orbiting it; the first person known to have proposed it was Aristarchus of Samos, c. 270 BCE. His writings on it are lost, but his contemporary…

haber-process.s: The Haber process, or Haber–Bosch process, is the main industrial method of making ammonia, combining nitrogen from the air with hydrogen over an iron catalyst; the German chemist Fritz Haber demonstrated it in the laboratory in 1909, and Carl Bosch scaled it up for BASF. The…

hippocratic-corpus.s: The Hippocratic Corpus is a collection of around 60 early Greek medical works associated with the physician Hippocrates, most written in the last decades of the 5th century BCE and the first half of the 4th; none is proven to be his own. Composed in Ionic Greek by many…

helots.s: The helots were a subjugated group who formed most of the population of Laconia and Messenia, the territories ruled by Sparta; tied to the land, they farmed it to support the Spartan citizens. Ancient writers disagreed on their status: Critias called them "slaves to the…

hyakusho.s: The hyakushō, the peasants, came second in shinōkōshō, the Confucian scheme of four occupations adopted from China: samurai, peasants, craftsmen and merchants. In Tokugawa Japan peasants were the great majority of the people, usually put at about 80 per cent, under a…

hinin.s: The hinin, literally "non-humans", were an outcast group of Edo-period Japan (1603–1868), placed with the kawata (called eta in official documents, a term now a slur) outside the social hierarchy. They were made to beg, perform in the streets and bury executed criminals, work…
